policy_title: Acupuncture for Chronic Lower Back Pain

extracted_content.title: Overview
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Overview
extracted_content.content: This policy establishes Humana's billing requirements and reimbursement guidelines, for 2022 and later, for the Medicare Part B benefit for acupuncture for chronic lower back pain (cLBP). Note: Some Humana Medicare Advantage (MA) plans have a supplemental benefit that covers acupuncture services that Original Medicare would not cover. This policy does not apply to services provided under one of those benefits.

extracted_content.title: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. Humana MA plans cover dry needling and acupuncture services under the acupuncture for cLBP benefit for the same diagnoses as Original Medicare. Except where noted below, providers must report acupuncture for cLBP services consistent with guidance in applicable Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) published transmittals and Internet-only Manuals. Except where noted below, Humana MA plans allow acupuncture for cLBP services consistent with the applicable CMS guidance for the date of service.

extracted_content.title: Practitioner Type
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Practitioner Type
extracted_content.content: For dates of service on or after January 1, 2022, Humana MA plans' acupuncture for cLBP benefit is not limited to services provided only by practitioner types that can provide services under Original Medicare's acupuncture coverage. Instead, Humana MA plans permit practitioners who satisfy all applicable acupuncture licensure and plan requirements, such as plan participation requirements, to submit claims for services for acupuncture for cLBP.

extracted_content.title: Number of Sessions
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Number of Sessions
extracted_content.content: Humana treats all services covered under the acupuncture for cLBP benefit furnished the same day as if they were furnished in one session. For 2022 and later, Humana MA plans cover up to 20 sessions per year. Therefore, Humana MA plans do not require providers to report modifier KX for charges for acupuncture visits 13 through 20 in any calendar year, despite CMS acupuncture billing guidance, for Original Medicare, about modifier KX billing. Note: For 2022 through 2025, the 20-session limitation does not apply to services rendered by the patient's primary care provider (PCP). extracted_content.title: Overview
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Overview
extracted_content.content: An ambulance is a professionally operated vehicle, provided by a licensed ambulance service, equipped for the transportation of a sick or injured person to or from the nearest medical facility qualified to treat the person's sickness or bodily injury. This policy establishes Humana's billing requirements and reimbursement for ambulance services.

extracted_content.title: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. Humana Medicare Advantage (MA) plans allow medically necessary ground ambulance and fixed or rotary wing air ambulance services according to Original Medicare guidelines. Humana only reimburses for covered transportation and mileage charges. The amount allowed for transportation includes reimbursement for all other items and services provided. Humana does not make separate payment for such items and services, including but not limited to oxygen, drugs, extra attendants, supplies, electrocardiograms (ECG or EKG) and night differential. Ambulance transportation provided to a member while registered as an inpatient at a hospital or skilled nursing facility (SNF), if billed, must be included in the facility's related consolidated inpatient claim. Charges for transportation of an inpatient will only be considered for reimbursement within the adjudication of the inpatient stay itself. In some situations, Humana determines that, though transportation was medically necessary, the mode of transportation may not have been medically necessary, such as transportation by air. When Humana determines that transportation was medically necessary, but air transportation was not medically necessary, Humana allows ground ambulance rates for the transportation. Generally, reimbursement for ambulance mileage to a facility is limited to the distance from the place from which the patient was transported to the nearest appropriate facility. However, when Humana authorizes admission to a facility in advance, regardless of whether prior authorization is required, Humana reimburses for mileage for the related ambulance transportation to that facility. A provider should bill all of the coverable mileage with HCPCS code A0425, A0435 or A0436. However, if a provider bills such mileage with HCPCS code A0888, Humana will not reimburse that charge but will deny it to provider liability. If the facility did not obtain prior authorization from Humana for the related admission, a provider should bill mileage for transportation beyond the closest facility with HCPCS code A0888. Humana will not reimburse that charge but will deny it to provider liability. Humana adjusts reimbursement of covered transportation and mileage charges when multiple patients are simultaneously transported in the same ambulance to the same destination, indicated by modifier GM. If two patients are transported, Humana allows 75 percent of the provider's contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member's plan for transportation and 50 percent of the provider's contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member's plan for mileage. If three patients are transported, Humana allows 60 percent of the provider's contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member's plan for transportation and a prorated percent of the provider's contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member's plan for mileage, based on the number of patients on board. Note: Some Humana MA plans have supplemental transportation benefits, which provide coverage of some transportation services that Original Medicare would not cover. Providers and members are advised to contact Humana to verify if a Humana MA plan has supplemental transportation benefits.

extracted_content.title: Billing
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Billing
extracted_content.content: Providers must bill appropriate modifiers with ambulance charges. Ambulance origin and destination modifiers are billed with both the transportation and mileage charges. When reporting ambulance origin and destination modifiers, the first letter represents the place of origin, and the second letter represents the destination. If a patient is pronounced dead after the ambulance is dispatched but before being loaded on board, providers must report modifier QL with the transportation charge rather than ambulance origin and destination modifiers. In such circumstances, mileage is not covered. However, if providers report the mileage charge, it must be billed with modifier QL, and it is not reimbursed. If multiple patients are simultaneously transported in the same ambulance to the same destination, providers must report modifier GM with the transportation and mileage charges.

extracted_content.title: Billing
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Billing
extracted_content.content: Providers must bill the ZIP code of the point of pickup (POP). For transportation for less than 100 miles, ambulance mileage may be reported in fractional units to the nearest tenth of a mile. When more than one hospital-to-hospital ambulance service is provided on the same day, the provider must submit a charge for each segment of transportation on a separate claim line with a unit of 1.

extracted_content.title: Additional provision for out-of-network providers
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Additional provision for out-of-network providers
extracted_content.content: 42 CFR 422.214 requires an out-of-network provider to accept, as payment in full, the amount the provider could collect if the patient were enrolled in Original Medicare. The provider can collect from the MA plan member the cost-sharing amount required under the MA plan and collect the remainder of the allowed amount from the MA plan.

extracted_content.title: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. The following policy applies to professional services only.

extracted_content.title: Reporting Anesthesia Services
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Reporting Anesthesia Services
extracted_content.content: Humana requires anesthesia services to be reported using a Current Procedural Terminology (CPT®) code in the 00100 - 01999 range.

extracted_content.title: Anesthesia Reimbursement Calculation
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Anesthesia Reimbursement Calculation
extracted_content.content: Humana plans calculate the reimbursement of anesthesia services with consideration to the base value units for the procedure, time units, modifiers and the conversion factor. The formula is as follows: (CMS Base Value Unit + Time Units + Anesthesia Physical Status Modifier Unit, if applicable) x Conversion Factor = Anesthesia Allowable. Note: Some anesthesia services are not time-based; therefore, this calculation does not apply to such services.

extracted_content.title: Reporting Anesthesia Time
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Reporting Anesthesia Time
extracted_content.content: Humana requires actual anesthesia time to be reported in one-minute increments in the anesthesia minutes field. Note: Some anesthesia services are not time-based and are excluded from this requirement.

extracted_content.title: Common Modifiers for Anesthesia Claims
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Common Modifiers for Anesthesia Claims
extracted_content.content: Humana requires the anesthesia service code to be appended, as appropriate, with modifier AA, AD, QK, QX, QY or QZ. For an allowed anesthesia charge submitted with modifiers AA, QK, QX, QY or QZ, Humana plans allow the following percentage of the provider's contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member's plan:

extracted_content.title: Medicare Advantage
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Medicare Advantage
extracted_content.content: reimbursement AA 100% QK 50% QX 50% QY 50% QZ 100% Note: Reimbursement of an anesthesia charge shall not exceed 100 percent of the total amount allowed for a single service reported on multiple providers' claims, such as when an anesthesiologist directs a nonphysician anesthetist. Additionally, for any coverable single anesthesia service, Humana plans allow no more than one anesthesiologist charge and allow no more than one nonphysician anesthetist charge. Humana calculates the reimbursement of an allowed anesthesia charge submitted with modifier AD with three base units, regardless of the base value units of the procedure code, multiplied by the conversion factor. One additional unit is considered when documentation confirms the supervising physician was present at induction. Additional units for length of time, qualifying circumstances codes or physical status modifiers are not allowed. Monitored anesthesia care must be indicated using modifier G8, G9 or QS, with the monitored anesthesia care modifier reported after modifier AA, AD, QK, QX, QY or QZ.

extracted_content.title: Anesthesia Physical Status Modifiers
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Anesthesia Physical Status Modifiers
extracted_content.content: Humana plans do not allow additional units for physical status modifiers P1 - P6. Physical status modifiers should be reported after modifier AA, AD, QK, QX, QY or QZ.

extracted_content.title: Qualifying Circumstance Codes
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Qualifying Circumstance Codes
extracted_content.content: Humana plans do not allow additional units for qualifying circumstance codes CPT codes 99100, 99116, 99135 and 99140.

reimbursement_guidelines.title: Reimbursement Guidelines
reimbursement_guidelines.content:
Humana plans calculate the reimbursement of anesthesia services with consideration to the base value units for the procedure, time units, modifiers and the conversion factor. The formula is as follows: (CMS Base Value Unit + Time Units + Anesthesia Physical Status Modifier Unit, if applicable) x Conversion Factor = Anesthesia Allowable. Note: Some anesthesia services are not time-based; therefore, this calculation does not apply to such services.

A medically necessary anesthesia procedure, such as an epidural injection or nerve block, administered with the intent to manage post-operative pain, may be reimbursed separately when the adequacy of the intra-operative anesthesia is not dependent on the epidural injection or nerve block. All the following requirements must be satisfied to qualify for separate reimbursement from the intra-operative anesthesia:

Medical record documentation of the post-operative pain management procedure must:

In certain circumstances additional payment rules may apply, including but not limited to the following:

When multiple procedures are performed on the same patient during a single anesthesia session, only the anesthesia service code with the highest base unit value should be reported. The combined time for all procedures should be reported with that code.

Humana plans do not reimburse for anesthesia services reported by the attending surgeon.

definitions.title: Definitions
definitions.content:
Base maximum amount payable under the member's plan: The maximum amount of reimbursement for a covered expense, determined by the member's plan. Depending on the plan, this may be the maximum allowable fee, the appropriate Medicare fee schedule rate or an amount derived from another payment model. Actual plan reimbursement may be less than this base maximum amount, because of applicable adjustments.

Conversion factor: The conversion factor is the multiplier that transforms relative values into payment amounts as shown in the CONV FACTOR field in the Medicare Physician Fee Schedule Relative Value File for the appropriate year.

CPT code 99100: Anesthesia for patient of extreme age, younger than 1 year and older than 70 (List separately in addition to code for primary anesthesia procedure).

CPT code 99116: Anesthesia complicated by utilization of total body hypothermia (List separately in addition to code for primary anesthesia procedure).

CPT code 99135: Anesthesia complicated by utilization of controlled hypotension (List separately in addition to code for primary anesthesia procedure).

CPT code 99140: Anesthesia complicated by emergency conditions (specify) (List separately in addition to code for primary anesthesia procedure).

Medicare Physician Fee Schedule (MPFS) Relative Value File: A file published by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services that includes, among other information, multiple procedure indicator, relative value units and conversion factors for physician services. This file is commonly referred to as the relative value unit (RVU) table.

Modifier AA: Anesthesia services performed personally by anesthesiologist.

Modifier AD: Medical supervision by physician: more than four concurrent anesthesia procedures.

Modifier G8: Monitored anesthesia care (MAC) for deep complex, complicated, or markedly invasive surgical procedures.

Modifier G9: Monitored anesthesia care for patient who has history of severe cardio-pulmonary condition.

Modifier P1: A normal healthy patient.

Modifier P2: A patient with mild systemic disease.

Modifier P3: A patient with severe systemic disease.

Modifier P4: A patient with severe systemic disease that is a constant threat to life.

Modifier P5: A moribund patient who is not expected to survive without the operation.

Modifier P6: A declared brain-dead patient whose organs are being removed for donor purposes.

Modifier QK: Medical direction of two, three, or four concurrent anesthesia procedures involving qualified individuals.

Modifier QS: Monitored anesthesia care service.

Modifier QX: CRNA service: with medical direction by a physician.

Modifier QY: Medical direction of one certified registered nurse anesthetist (CRNA) by an anesthesiologist.

Modifier QZ: CRNA service: without medical direction by a physician.

extracted_content.title: Overview
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Overview
extracted_content.content: According to the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), assistant at surgery services are those services rendered by physicians or nonphysician practitioners (NPPs) who actively assist the physician in charge of performing a surgical procedure.

extracted_content.title: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements.

extracted_content.title: Coverage
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Coverage
extracted_content.content: Original Medicare (OM) covers an assistant at surgery service provided by a physician, with some exclusions, or an NPP. A charge for an assistant at surgery service provided by another individual is not payable. Therefore, a Humana Medicare Advantage (MA) plan denies, to provider liability, a charge for an assistant at surgery service submitted by an individual whose service would not be coverable for an enrollee of OM. Humana uses the Medicare Physician Fee Schedule (MPFS) Relative Value File assistant at surgery indicator to determine if an assistant at surgery is medically necessary and, therefore, covered. When the MPFS Relative Value File is not definitive, then Humana's internal criteria are used.

extracted_content.subsection: Assistant at Surgery in a Teaching Hospital
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Coverage > Assistant at Surgery in a Teaching Hospital
extracted_content.content: Humana determines coverage of a charge submitted by an assistant at surgery in a teaching hospital consistent with the qualifications required by CMS for an OM enrollee.

extracted_content.title: Billing
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Coverage > Billing
extracted_content.content: Only one of the following modifiers should be billed per charge: AS, 80, 81 or 82. An assistant at surgery should bill the same procedure code as the primary surgeon and the appropriate assistant at surgery modifier, except when billing for assistance during a cesarean delivery. When billing for assistance only during a cesarean delivery, the assistant at surgery should bill Current Procedural Terminology (CPT®) code 59514 (cesarean delivery only) or CPT code 59620 (cesarean delivery only, following attempted vaginal delivery after previous cesarean delivery) and the appropriate assistant at surgery modifier. Humana will not reimburse a practitioner who acts as an assistant at surgery in a cesarean delivery any more than the assistant at surgery rate that would apply for the CPT code appropriate for delivery only.

extracted_content.title: Reimbursement
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Coverage > Reimbursement
extracted_content.content: A Humana MA plan allows an assistant at surgery physician charge, indicated by modifier 80, 81 or 82, at 16 percent of the contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member's plan, subject to any other applicable reductions, for a service considered medically necessary. A Humana MA plan allows an assistant at surgery NPP charge, indicated by modifier AS, at 16 percent of the contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member's plan appropriate for the NPP, subject to any other applicable reductions, for a service considered medically necessary.

Humana uses the Medicare Physician Fee Schedule (MPFS) Relative Value File assistant at surgery indicator to determine if an assistant at surgery is medically necessary and, therefore, covered. When the MPFS Relative Value File is not definitive, then Humana's internal criteria are used.

Humana determines coverage of a charge submitted by an assistant at surgery in a teaching hospital consistent with the qualifications required by CMS for an OM enrollee.

Only one of the following modifiers should be billed per charge: AS, 80, 81 or 82. An assistant at surgery should bill the same procedure code as the primary surgeon and the appropriate assistant at surgery modifier, except when billing for assistance during a cesarean delivery. When billing for assistance only during a cesarean delivery, the assistant at surgery should bill Current Procedural Terminology (CPT®) code 59514 (cesarean delivery only) or CPT code 59620 (cesarean delivery only, following attempted vaginal delivery after previous cesarean delivery) and the appropriate assistant at surgery modifier. Humana will not reimburse a practitioner who acts as an assistant at surgery in a cesarean delivery any more than the assistant at surgery rate that would apply for the CPT code appropriate for delivery only.

A Humana MA plan allows an assistant at surgery physician charge, indicated by modifier 80, 81 or 82, at 16 percent of the contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member's plan, subject to any other applicable reductions, for a service considered medically necessary. A Humana MA plan allows an assistant at surgery NPP charge, indicated by modifier AS, at 16 percent of the contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member's plan appropriate for the NPP, subject to any other applicable reductions, for a service considered medically necessary.

Physician: The amount allowed is 16 percent of the provider's contracted rate, subject to other applicable adjustments.

XXXXX $1,000 $750 $750 x 16% = $120 NPP: The amount allowed is 16 percent of the provider's contracted rate, subject to other applicable adjustments.

XXXXX $1,500 $1,000 $1,000 x 16% = $160

Physician: The amount allowed is 16 percent of 100 percent of the MPFS amount for the service, subject to other applicable adjustments.

XXXXX $1,000 $750 $750 x 100% x 16% = $120 NPP: The amount allowed is 16 percent of 85 percent (13.6 percent) of the MPFS amount for the service, subject to other applicable adjustments.

XXXXX $1,500 $1,000 $1,000 x 85% x 16% = $136

Base maximum amount payable under the member's plan: The maximum amount of reimbursement for a covered expense, determined by the member's plan. Depending on the plan, this may be the maximum allowable fee, the appropriate Medicare fee schedule rate or an amount derived from another payment model. Actual plan reimbursement may be less than this base maximum amount, because of applicable adjustments.

Maximum allowable fee (MAF): The maximum amount of reimbursement for a covered expense, determined by the member's plan provisions. Actual plan payment may be less than MAF, because of applicable adjustments.

Medicare Physician Fee Schedule (MPFS) Relative Value File: A file published by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services that includes, among other information, assistant at surgery indicator, relative value units and conversion factors for physician services. This file is commonly referred to as the relative value unit (RVU) table.

extracted_content.title: Overview
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Overview
extracted_content.content: This policy outlines Humana's billing requirements and reimbursement for principal care management (PCM), chronic care management (CCM) and complex CCM services.

extracted_content.title: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. Humana Medicare Advantage (MA) plans may reimburse a PCM charge, CCM charge, or complex CCM charge when all of the applicable Medicare Program requirements are met. Humana requires a provider to follow all PCM and CCM requirements as outlined in the Federal Register and relevant CMS guidance. That includes, but is not limited to, the criteria outlined below.

extracted_content.title: Member Pre-Condition
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Member Pre-Condition
extracted_content.content: For PCM services, the member must be diagnosed with one chronic condition that places the patient at significant risk of death, acute exacerbation/decompensation or functional decline or that is expected to last at least 3 months or until the death of the patient. For CCM services, the member must be diagnosed with at least two chronic conditions that place the patient at significant risk of death, acute exacerbation/decompensation or functional decline and that are expected to last at least 12 months or until the death of the patient.

extracted_content.title: Staff Requirement
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Staff Requirement
extracted_content.content: PCM and CCM services must be performed by clinical staff meeting the requirements of auxiliary personnel as defined by 42 CFR 410.26(a)(1).

extracted_content.title: Billing Limitations
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Billing Limitations
extracted_content.content: A provider may not simultaneously bill for PCM services and certain other services, including CCM, for the same member. A provider may not bill for PCM services during the surgical global period of a service for which they are reimbursed for the same member. Only one provider may bill for CCM services for a specific member per month. CCM services for a specific member must be billed for either CCM or complex CCM, but not both, per month. A provider may not bill for CCM services rendered to a member during an inpatient facility stay that is coverable by the member's MA plan.

extracted_content.content: Humana's Making it Easier web-based training series includes a video on the proper reporting and reimbursement of CCM and PCM services that may supplement your understanding of this policy.

In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. Humana Medicare Advantage (MA) plans may reimburse a PCM charge, CCM charge, or complex CCM charge when all of the applicable Medicare Program requirements are met. Humana requires a provider to follow all PCM and CCM requirements as outlined in the Federal Register and relevant CMS guidance. That includes, but is not limited to, the criteria outlined below.

For PCM services, the member must be diagnosed with one chronic condition that places the patient at significant risk of death, acute exacerbation/decompensation or functional decline or that is expected to last at least 3 months or until the death of the patient. For CCM services, the member must be diagnosed with at least two chronic conditions that place the patient at significant risk of death, acute exacerbation/decompensation or functional decline and that are expected to last at least 12 months or until the death of the patient.

PCM and CCM services must be performed by clinical staff meeting the requirements of auxiliary personnel as defined by 42 CFR 410.26(a)(1).

A provider may not simultaneously bill for PCM services and certain other services, including CCM, for the same member. A provider may not bill for PCM services during the surgical global period of a service for which they are reimbursed for the same member. Only one provider may bill for CCM services for a specific member per month. CCM services for a specific member must be billed for either CCM or complex CCM, but not both, per month. A provider may not bill for CCM services rendered to a member during an inpatient facility stay that is coverable by the member's MA plan.

Humana's Making it Easier web-based training series includes a video on the proper reporting and reimbursement of CCM and PCM services that may supplement your understanding of this policy.

extracted_content.title: Overview
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Overview
extracted_content.content: Humana adjudicates a claim for services provided to a plan member based on the information submitted in that claim and information related to that claim. If a qualified healthcare provider disagrees with Humana's adjudication of that claim, based on the information submitted in that claim, that provider may submit to Humana a request for a dispute review of the plan's determination. If a provider submits a request for a dispute review timely and with all required information, Humana will review the claim to determine whether to revise the adjudication. Humana plans may use medical records and other available relevant documentation to review a dispute. This policy establishes the applicable timeframe for a qualified healthcare provider submission of a dispute request. Note: A corrected claim is a provider's submission of information that constitutes a material change to an existing claim. A claim submission that constitutes a material change to an existing claim is not a disagreement about Humana's adjudication of the claim as based on the information in the previous claim submission. Therefore, Humana plans will not review a corrected claim as a dispute.

extracted_content.content: Unless otherwise stated in the contract, an in-network qualified healthcare provider may submit a dispute request within 18 months from the receipt of the original claim determination. An out-of-network qualified healthcare provider does not have a contractual relationship with a particular plan that would afford that qualified healthcare provider direct rights against that plan. An out-of-network qualified healthcare provider lacks, for example, the right to submit a claim, the right to require the plan to process a claim seeking a member's plan or policy benefits, the right to submit a dispute request and the right to submit corrected claims. A dispute can be requested when a provider disagrees with Humana's payment amount, payment denial or nonpayment of a claim. *In cases where Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), state Medicaid programs or state mandates use definition(s) that differ from those provided above, Humana will defer to their definition(s). How to make a claim-payment inquiry or submit an appeal or dispute Online: Appeals and disputes for finalized Humana Medicare Advantage, Medicaid or commercial claims can be submitted through Availity's secure provider portal, Availity EssentialsTM. To get started: 1. Sign in to Availity Essentials. 2. This adds the claim to your Appeals worklist but does not submit it to Humana. 3. You can submit the appeal or dispute to Humana immediately or wait until later and submit it from your Appeals worklist. 4. To access your Appeals worklist at any time, go to "Claims & Payments," then select "Appeals." definitions.title: Definitions
definitions.content:
An appeal is a formal request to change an adverse determination. When a provider is submitting an appeal on behalf of a member, an Appointment of Representative form is required.

A claim-payment inquiry is made when a provider has a question regarding how a claim processed.

A dispute can be requested when a provider disagrees with Humana's payment amount, payment denial or nonpayment of a claim.

*In cases where Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), state Medicaid programs or state

mandates use definition(s) that differ from those provided above, Humana will defer to their definition(s). How to make a claim-payment inquiry or submit an appeal or dispute Online: Appeals and disputes for finalized Humana Medicare Advantage, Medicaid or commercial claims can be submitted through Availity's secure provider portal, Availity EssentialsTM. To get started:

1. Sign in to Availity Essentials.

2. Use the Claim Status tool to locate the claim you want to appeal or dispute, and then select

the Dispute Claim button on the claim details screen. This adds the claim to your Appeals worklist but does not submit it to Humana.

3. You can submit the appeal or dispute to Humana immediately or wait until later and

submit it from your Appeals worklist.

4. To access your Appeals worklist at any time, go to "Claims & Payments," then select

"Appeals." Additional details can be found at Manage claim appeals and disputes online.

• Availity Essentials resources:

- For training, visit Humana.com/ProviderWebinars.

2 642103ALL0125 (HUMP642103) GHHKBLLEN

- Find helpful resources on how to use Availity tools and features by signing in to

Availity Essentials and using the Help & Training menu located on the main navigation bar.

- Find help with technical website issues by calling Availity Client Services at

800-AVAILITY (282-4548), Monday - Friday, 8 a.m. - 8 p.m., Eastern time. Mail: You can submit claim disputes via mail to:

Please be sure to include:

1. The healthcare provider's name and Tax Identification Number (TIN).

2. The member's Humana ID number and relationship to the patient.

3. The date of service, claim number and name of the provider.

4. The charge amount, actual payment amount, expected payment amount and a description of

the basis for the contestation.

5. Contact information for Humana's response.

Phone claim-payment inquiry: Call Humana's provider call center at 800-448-6262. Our representatives are trained to answer many of your claim questions and can initiate contact with other Humana departments when further review or research is needed. For Medicare specific claims, see chart below:

For Medicaid specific claims, refer to this chart for the appropriate state: Contact Information for Humana Providers | Humana.

Note the reference number issued to you by the provider call center representative, as it will be needed in the future.

If your issue is still outstanding and has not been adequately addressed by the call center representative, you have the option to speak to a provider call center supervisor. Based on availability, you will be connected to a supervisor, or a supervisor will contact you within

3 642103ALL0125 (HUMP642103) GHHKBLLEN 48 hours of your request.

In some situations, the call center representative will route your issue to an internal team at Humana. If this occurs, you will receive a letter or updated explanation of remittance from the Humana department that completes the additional review/research. Most inquiries receive a response in 30 to 45 days. Please allow us time to properly research and resolve your inquiry before contacting us again.

Escalations around Code Editing disputes and code edit denials should be submitted through Availity's secure provider portal, Availity Essentials.

1. Sign in to Availity Essentials (opens in new window) .

2. Use the Claim Status tool to locate the claim you want to appeal or dispute, and then select the

Dispute Claim button on the claim details screen. This adds the claim to your Appeals worklist but does not submit it to Humana.

3. You can submit the appeal or dispute to Humana immediately or wait until later and submit it from

your Appeals worklist.

4. To access your Appeals worklist at any time, go to "Claims & Payments," then select "Appeals."

If you are a participating provider and disagree with our determination after we respond to your initial online, mail or phone submission, you can escalate your concern. Send a secure email to HumanaProviderServices@humana.com. Include the Claim Escalation Form (opens in new window) with all necessary fields completed. List all reference number(s), interaction number(s) or invoice number(s) associated with previous attempt(s) to resolve the inquiry.

4 642103ALL0125 (HUMP642103) GHHKBLLEN Look for an "Acknowledgment of Submission" email with a tracking number within 5 business days of your submission. You will receive a follow-up email every 21 days thereafter.

Nonparticipating providers can find details on how to appeal determinations on Medical Claim Payment Reconsiderations and Appeals.

Follow any written instructions you receive for disputes on medical record reviews. For all other PPI inquiries about overpayment-related items or escalated concerns, follow the instructions below. Additional guidance can be found at Humana.com/PPI. For initial PPI inquiries, you can contact us: Online:

electronically with the online overpayment application on Availity Essentials at www.availity.com under "Claims & Payments."

Essentials. Sign in to Availity Essentials and select the Humana tile under Payer Spaces. Select "Medical Records Management" under the Applications tab to launch the tool.

2432 Fortune Drive, Suite 200

reimbursement_guidelines.content:
In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. Unless Humana policy or guidance directs otherwise, Humana requires providers to bill codes and other claims data according to the following:

1. Applicable Original Medicare and Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) guidance, if any; or

2. Otherwise, the applicable industry standard established by the appropriate authority. Examples include:

Current Procedural Terminology (CPT) coding standards by the American Medical Association (AMA);

837 electronic transaction standards by the American National Standards Institute (ANSI) X12;

International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision, Clinical Modifications (ICD-10-CM) coding standards by the

Standards for reporting institutional claims by the National Uniform Billing Committee (NUBC).

extracted_content.content: A modifier is a two-character code appended to a Current Procedural Terminology (CPT®) code or Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System (HCPCS) code to clarify the services rendered without changing the procedure code. Modifiers can facilitate editing, increase accuracy in reimbursement and improve coding consistency. Documentation of services must support a submitted modifier.

extracted_content.content: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. Humana plans require the use of CPT and HCPCS modifiers when appropriate. If a modifier is submitted, the claim is subject to review to ensure the procedure code and modifier combination is correct and the modifier was necessary. If modifiers are submitted inappropriately, the claim line is denied or payment recovery will occur. Below is a list of some commonly used modifiers, a high-level explanation of how those modifiers are generally used for reimbursement and general reporting information. extracted_content.title: Overview
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Overview
extracted_content.content: This policy establishes Humana's expectations regarding cost-sharing for cost-share protected members.

extracted_content.title: Medicare Advantage and Medicaid Payment Policy
extracted_content.subsection: Medicare Advantage and Medicaid Payment Policy
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: References > Medicare Advantage and Medicaid Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. Some members are cost-share protected under federal law, meaning that providers must not collect from those members the calculated cost-sharing for covered services. Though the collection of cost-sharing from a member might be forbidden, if there is a payer subsequent to Humana, it might be possible to collect that cost-sharing from that subsequent payer. Humana uses remittance advice remark codes (RARCs) to indicate that members are cost-share protected. For example, a specific RARC's definition might be, "Alert: Patient is a Medicaid/Qualified Medicare Beneficiary. Review your records for any wrongfully collected deductible. This amount may be billed to a subsequent payer." A provider should note when a Humana electronic remittance advice (ERA) includes such a RARC and react to it appropriately.

policy_title: Dental Services Inextricably Linked to Medical Services

extracted_content.title: Overview
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Overview
extracted_content.content: Dental services are generally not covered by the Medicare Program's basic benefits. However, one exception for this coverage exclusion is for dental services that are inextricably linked to the clinical success of a covered medical service. In such cases, there must also be exchange of information, or integration, between the medical professional and the dentist. This policy establishes Humana's billing requirements and reimbursement for dental services that are inextricably linked to the clinical success of a covered medical service.

extracted_content.title: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. This policy applies to dental services submitted for coverage under the medical benefit.

extracted_content.title: Modifier KX
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Modifier KX
extracted_content.content: For dates of services beginning July 1, 2025, Humana Medicare Advantage (MA) plans require providers to append modifier KX to a Current Dental Terminology (CDT) code to indicate that the dental service is inextricably linked to a covered medical service and that there has been integration between the medical and dental providers. Humana may deny a claim for a CDT code that is not reported with modifier KX. For dates of service before July 1, 2025, Humana encourages providers to report modifier KX for such services.

extracted_content.title: Diagnosis Codes
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Diagnosis Codes
extracted_content.content: For dates of service beginning July 1, 2025, Humana MA plans require providers to report diagnosis codes on all claims for dental services. Humana denies claims for dental services if the claim does not include diagnosis coding. For dates of service before July 1, 2025, Humana encourages providers to report diagnosis codes on all claims for dental services.

extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Definitions of Italicized Terms
extracted_content.content: Modifier KX: Requirements specified in the medical policy have been met.

reimbursement_guidelines.title: Reimbursement Guidelines
reimbursement_guidelines.content:
In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. This policy applies to dental services submitted for coverage under the medical benefit.

For dates of services beginning July 1, 2025, Humana Medicare Advantage (MA) plans require providers to append modifier KX to a Current Dental Terminology (CDT) code to indicate that the dental service is inextricably linked to a covered medical service and that there has been integration between the medical and dental providers. Humana may deny a claim for a CDT code that is not reported with modifier KX. For dates of service before July 1, 2025, Humana encourages providers to report modifier KX for such services.

For dates of service beginning July 1, 2025, Humana MA plans require providers to report diagnosis codes on all claims for dental services. Humana denies claims for dental services if the claim does not include diagnosis coding. For dates of service before July 1, 2025, Humana encourages providers to report diagnosis codes on all claims for dental services.

Modifier KX: Requirements specified in the medical policy have been met.

extracted_content.title: General Policy Guidelines
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > General Policy Guidelines
extracted_content.content: Humana Medicare Advantage (MA) plans generally allow DME according to the applicable Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) guidance. Except where guidance in this policy differs from Original Medicare, providers should follow the applicable CMS guidance. For a DME item that can be rented or purchased, whether that item is rented or purchased is subject to any applicable referral or prior authorization determination. For a DME item that can be rented, when the Medicare Durable Medical Equipment, Prosthetics, Orthotics and Supplies (DMEPOS) Fee Schedule has no rental rate for that item, Humana will apply a contracted rental rate, where applicable. If there is no contracted rental rate, Humana may allow the item at the purchase rate. For a DME item that can be purchased, the amount allowed is affected by which purchase modifier is reported.

extracted_content.title: General Policy Guidelines
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > General Policy Guidelines
extracted_content.content: If a charge for a covered DME item is submitted with modifier NU, the amount allowed is the new equipment purchase rate.

extracted_content.title: General Policy Guidelines
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > General Policy Guidelines
extracted_content.content: If a charge for a covered DME item is submitted with modifier UE, the amount allowed is the used equipment purchase rate. The amount allowed for purchased used equipment is a reduced rate, typically 75%, of the new equipment purchase rate. Reimbursement for the DME item includes reimbursement for delivery and set-up. Humana does not reimburse separately for delivery and set-up. Reimbursement for covered services provided to an MA member is subject to the same special pricing rules that would apply for covered services provided to Original Medicare enrollees. For example, if a covered service provided to an Original Medicare enrollee would be priced using the Competitive Bidding Program rate, then that service provided to a Humana MA member in the same competitive bidding area is reimbursed using the same rate. Specific Guidelines for DME Items Categorized as Capped Rental DME Items Humana requires an appropriate capped rental modifier and transaction modifier. Humana determines the amount allowed based on the transaction modifier billed for an item categorized as a capped rental DME item as described below.

extracted_content.title: Rental
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Rental
extracted_content.content: If a charge for a covered capped rental DME item is submitted with modifier RR, the amount allowed is the monthly rental rate, as described below. Rental is allowed for a period of continuous use not to exceed 13 months. Reimbursement to a provider whose contract is not based on the Medicare DMEPOS Fee Schedule is allowed at the contracted rental rate. Otherwise, Humana allows an item, other than a power wheelchair, at a monthly rental rate of 10% of the item's purchase rate for each of the first three months and then 7.5% of the purchase rate for the remainder of the rental period. For a power wheelchair, Humana allows at a monthly rental rate of 15% of the item's purchase rate for the first three months and then 6% of the purchase rate for the remainder of the rental period. In both scenarios, the monthly rental rate is based on the purchase rate in effect for the date of service billed. A capped rental DME item is considered purchased after 13 continuous months of covered rental. Humana reserves the right to allow at the purchase rate at any time, regardless of the submission of modifier RR. In such cases, the amount allowed is either the new equipment purchase rate or used equipment purchase rate, as described in the General Policy Guidelines section of this policy.

extracted_content.title: Equipment
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Equipment
extracted_content.content: Humana allows reimbursement for rental of oxygen equipment for a period of continuous use not to exceed 36 months. Only one supplier is reimbursed per month. If there is a change in supplier or a change in the type of stationary oxygen equipment supplied, the same 36-month rental period continues. If both stationary and portable equipment are used, each is allowed through 36 continuous months. If there is a gap in service of 60 days or more during a 36-month rental period, a new 36-month rental period begins. If there is a gap in service for fewer than 60 days, the original 36-month rental period continues. Humana requires modifier RR for rental of oxygen equipment. The amount allowed is the monthly rental rate. The monthly rental rate may be subject to adjustment depending on the amount of oxygen prescribed and whether portable oxygen has been prescribed. In such circumstances, Humana also requires a provider to report one of the following modifiers, as supported by the prescription: modifier QA, QB, QE, QF, QG or QR. Humana determines the amount allowed as follows:

extracted_content.title: Equipment
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Equipment
extracted_content.content: If a charge for stationary equipment is submitted with modifier QA or QE, the amount allowed is 50% of the monthly rental rate.

extracted_content.title: Equipment
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Equipment
extracted_content.content: If a charge for stationary equipment is submitted with modifier QG or QR, the amount allowed is 150% of the monthly rental rate.

extracted_content.title: Equipment
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Equipment
extracted_content.content: If a charge for portable equipment is submitted with modifier QF or QB, the amount allowed is the greater of 50% of the monthly rental rate for stationary equipment or 100% of the monthly rental rate for portable equipment.

extracted_content.title: Equipment Replacement
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Equipment Replacement
extracted_content.content: A new 36-month rental period may begin if the oxygen equipment has been lost, stolen or unintentionally damaged beyond repair or has met the reasonable useful lifetime (RUL) of at least five years. The RUL begins with the initial month's rental. For additional guidance, see the Repair and Replacement section of this policy.

extracted_content.content: Portable contents are not separately reimbursable if there is an allowed, same-month stationary equipment charge or stationary contents charge. Reimbursement for maintenance and servicing does not include reimbursement for contents. Therefore, contents are separately reimbursable when billed the same month as maintenance and servicing.

extracted_content.title: Supplies and Accessories
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Supplies and Accessories
extracted_content.content: Reimbursement for the rental of stationary or portable oxygen equipment includes reimbursement for oxygen supplies and accessories. Humana does not reimburse separately for oxygen supplies and accessories until after the 36-month rental period has ended.

extracted_content.title: Maintenance and Servicing
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Maintenance and Servicing
extracted_content.content: Humana allows reimbursement for maintenance and servicing of certain concentrators and refilling equipment, indicated by modifier MS, once every six months beginning the later of six months after the 36-month rental period or six months from the manufacturer's warranty expiration. Humana does not allow reimbursement for maintenance and servicing of gaseous and liquid equipment.

extracted_content.title: Acute Post-Operative Pain
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Acute Post-Operative Pain
extracted_content.content: Humana allows a one-month rental period if a TENS unit is used to treat acute post-operative pain. The supplier must submit the charge with modifier RR.

extracted_content.title: Chronic Pain
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Chronic Pain
extracted_content.content: Humana requires an appropriate transaction modifier. Humana determines the amount allowed based on the transaction modifier billed for a TENS unit as described below. Humana requires a two-month rental trial period to assess an individual's suitability for ongoing treatment if a TENS unit is used to treat chronic pain. The supplier must submit charges for the two-month rental trial period with modifier RR. If the TENS unit is approved for on-going rental or purchase, the applicable rental rate or purchase amount will be allowed as described below.

extracted_content.title: Rental
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Rental
extracted_content.content: If the TENS unit is approved for on-going use, and the charge is submitted with modifier RR, the amount allowed is the monthly rental rate. However, Humana reserves the right to allow at the purchase rate at any time, regardless of the submission of modifier RR. Rental is allowed for a period of continuous use not to exceed 13 months. The two-month rental trial period does not count towards the 13-month rental period. After the two-month rental trial period, the TENS unit is considered purchased in the month in which the total of all amounts allowed, for one or multiple charges, reaches the applicable purchase amount or exceeds the 13-month rental period.

extracted_content.title: Purchase
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Purchase
extracted_content.content: If the TENS unit is approved for on-going use, and the unit is purchased, the supplier must submit the charge with the appropriate purchase modifier. The amount allowed is either the new equipment purchase rate or used equipment purchase rate, as described in the General Policy Guidelines section of this policy, for the month billed. If the item was previously rented, then the purchase rate is based on the purchase rate in effect at the time of the first month's rental. The two-month rental trial period does not count towards the purchase amount. After the two-month rental trial period, the TENS unit is considered purchased in the month in which the total of all amounts allowed, for one or multiple charges, reaches the applicable purchase amount or exceeds the 13-month rental period. Specific Guidelines for DME Items Categorized as Inexpensive or Routinely Purchased (IRP) DME Items Although transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulator (TENS) units qualify as items of IRP DME, reimbursement for TENS units differs. See the Transcutaneous Electrical Nerve Stimulator section of this policy. Humana requires an appropriate transaction modifier. Humana determines the amount allowed based on the transaction modifier billed for an item categorized as IRP DME as described below.

extracted_content.content: If a charge for a covered IRP DME item is submitted with modifier RR, the amount allowed is the monthly rental rate. However, Humana reserves the right to allow at the purchase rate at any time, regardless of the submission of modifier RR. An IRP DME item is considered purchased in the month in which the total of all amounts allowed equals the applicable purchase amount for that item.

extracted_content.content: Humana may reimburse the replacement of a DME base item, part or accessory after the expiration of the RUL if it is still medically necessary but no longer functional. The RUL period begins the first date of service when the specific base item, part or accessory was individually reimbursed. Additionally, the following criteria must be met:

extracted_content.content: Base item, part or accessory replacement is not due to intentional damage, neglect or misuse of equipment.

extracted_content.content: Replacement of a part or accessory is only allowed for a member if the same member owns the base item.

extracted_content.content: The base item, part or accessory must not be under warranty. Documentation of an expired or denied warranty is required, upon request.

extracted_content.title: Repair and Replacement

extracted_content.content: The base item, part or accessory is not currently being rented.

extracted_content.subsection: Replacement Prior to the Expiration of the RUL
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Replacement Prior to the Expiration of the RUL
extracted_content.content: In addition to the relevant requirements outlined above, the following conditions apply to replacement of a DME base item, part or accessory before expiration of the RUL.

extracted_content.content: Humana may reimburse the replacement of a base item, part or accessory before expiration of the RUL only if either of the following scenarios are true:

extracted_content.title: Modifier RA
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Modifier RA
extracted_content.content: The member's medical needs have changed such that a different item is medically necessary; or

extracted_content.title: Modifier RA
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Modifier RA
extracted_content.content: The item was lost, stolen or unintentionally damaged beyond repair. For only the first charge for the replacement item, modifier RA must be billed with the Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System (HCPCS) code for a base item, part or accessory replaced for one of the scenarios described above.

extracted_content.content: Humana may reimburse the replacement of a part or accessory in association with the covered repair of a base item before the expiration of the RUL of the part or accessory when the following criteria are met:

reimbursement_guidelines.title: Reimbursement Guidelines
reimbursement_guidelines.content:
Specific Guidelines for DME Items Categorized as Capped Rental DME Items

Specific Guidelines for DME Items Categorized as Inexpensive or Routinely Purchased DME Items

In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements.

Humana Medicare Advantage (MA) plans generally allow DME according to the applicable Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) guidance. Except where guidance in this policy differs from Original Medicare, providers should follow the applicable CMS guidance. For a DME item that can be rented or purchased, whether that item is rented or purchased is subject to any applicable referral or prior authorization determination. For a DME item that can be rented, when the Medicare Durable Medical Equipment, Prosthetics, Orthotics and Supplies (DMEPOS) Fee Schedule has no rental rate for that item, Humana will apply a contracted rental rate, where applicable. If there is no contracted rental rate, Humana may allow the item at the purchase rate. For a DME item that can be purchased, the amount allowed is affected by which purchase modifier is reported.

If a charge for a covered DME item is submitted with modifier NU, the amount allowed is the new equipment purchase rate.

If a charge for a covered DME item is submitted with modifier UE, the amount allowed is the used equipment purchase rate. The amount allowed for purchased used equipment is a reduced rate, typically 75%, of the new equipment purchase rate. Reimbursement for the DME item includes reimbursement for delivery and set-up. Humana does not reimburse separately for delivery and set-up. Reimbursement for covered services provided to an MA member is subject to the same special pricing rules that would apply for covered services provided to Original Medicare enrollees. For example, if a covered service provided to an Original Medicare enrollee would be priced using the Competitive Bidding Program rate, then that service provided to a Humana MA member in the same competitive bidding area is reimbursed using the same rate. Specific Guidelines for DME Items Categorized as Capped Rental DME Items Humana requires an appropriate capped rental modifier and transaction modifier. Humana determines the amount allowed based on the transaction modifier billed for an item categorized as a capped rental DME item as described below.

If a charge for a covered capped rental DME item is submitted with modifier RR, the amount allowed is the monthly rental rate, as described below. Rental is allowed for a period of continuous use not to exceed 13 months. Reimbursement to a provider whose contract is not based on the Medicare DMEPOS Fee Schedule is allowed at the contracted rental rate. Otherwise, Humana allows an item, other than a power wheelchair, at a monthly rental rate of 10% of the item's purchase rate for each of the first three months and then 7.5% of the purchase rate for the remainder of the rental period. For a power wheelchair, Humana allows at a monthly rental rate of 15% of the item's purchase rate for the first three months and then 6% of the purchase rate for the remainder of the rental period. In both scenarios, the monthly rental rate is based on the purchase rate in effect for the date of service billed. A capped rental DME item is considered purchased after 13 continuous months of covered rental. Humana reserves the right to allow at the purchase rate at any time, regardless of the submission of modifier RR. In such cases, the amount allowed is either the new equipment purchase rate or used equipment purchase rate, as described in the General Policy Guidelines section of this policy.

Humana generally allows a purchase option for an item that CMS defines as a complex, rehabilitative power wheelchair and for certain accessories, as defined by CMS, provided for use with that wheelchair. To indicate that a charge is for the purchase of a

capped rental DME item, the supplier must submit the charge with the appropriate purchase modifier. The amount allowed is either the new equipment purchase rate or used equipment purchase rate, as described in the General Policy Guidelines section of this policy.

Humana allows reimbursement for rental of oxygen equipment for a period of continuous use not to exceed 36 months. Only one supplier is reimbursed per month. If there is a change in supplier or a change in the type of stationary oxygen equipment supplied, the same 36-month rental period continues. If both stationary and portable equipment are used, each is allowed through 36 continuous months. If there is a gap in service of 60 days or more during a 36-month rental period, a new 36-month rental period begins. If there is a gap in service for fewer than 60 days, the original 36-month rental period continues. Humana requires modifier RR for rental of oxygen equipment. The amount allowed is the monthly rental rate. The monthly rental rate may be subject to adjustment depending on the amount of oxygen prescribed and whether portable oxygen has been prescribed. In such circumstances, Humana also requires a provider to report one of the following modifiers, as supported by the prescription: modifier QA, QB, QE, QF, QG or QR. Humana determines the amount allowed as follows:

If a charge for stationary equipment is submitted with modifier QA or QE, the amount allowed is 50% of the monthly rental rate.

If a charge for stationary equipment is submitted with modifier QG or QR, the amount allowed is 150% of the monthly rental rate.

If a charge for portable equipment is submitted with modifier QF or QB, the amount allowed is the greater of 50% of the monthly rental rate for stationary equipment or 100% of the monthly rental rate for portable equipment.

A new 36-month rental period may begin if the oxygen equipment has been lost, stolen or unintentionally damaged beyond repair or has met the reasonable useful lifetime (RUL) of at least five years. The RUL begins with the initial month's rental. For additional guidance, see the Repair and Replacement section of this policy.

Humana allows reimbursement for oxygen contents unless one or more of the following situations applies:

Contents are not reimbursable when, in the same month, only a concentrator is supplied.

Stationary contents are not separately reimbursable if there is an allowed, same-month stationary equipment charge.

Portable contents are not separately reimbursable if there is an allowed, same-month stationary equipment charge or stationary contents charge. Reimbursement for maintenance and servicing does not include reimbursement for contents. Therefore, contents are separately reimbursable when billed the same month as maintenance and servicing.

Reimbursement for the rental of stationary or portable oxygen equipment includes reimbursement for oxygen supplies and accessories. Humana does not reimburse separately for oxygen supplies and accessories until after the 36-month rental period has ended.

Humana allows reimbursement for maintenance and servicing of certain concentrators and refilling equipment, indicated by modifier MS, once every six months beginning the later of six months after the 36-month rental period or six months from the manufacturer's warranty expiration. Humana does not allow reimbursement for maintenance and servicing of gaseous and liquid equipment.

Specific Guidelines for DME Items Categorized as Transcutaneous Electrical Nerve Stimulator (TENS) Units

Humana allows a one-month rental period if a TENS unit is used to treat acute post-operative pain. The supplier must submit the charge with modifier RR.

Humana requires an appropriate transaction modifier. Humana determines the amount allowed based on the transaction modifier billed for a TENS unit as described below. Humana requires a two-month rental trial period to assess an individual's suitability for ongoing treatment if a TENS unit is used to treat chronic pain. The supplier must submit charges for the two-month rental trial period with modifier RR. If the TENS unit is approved for on-going rental or purchase, the applicable rental rate or purchase amount will be allowed as described below.

If the TENS unit is approved for on-going use, and the charge is submitted with modifier RR, the amount allowed is the monthly rental rate. However, Humana reserves the right to allow at the purchase rate at any time, regardless of the submission of modifier RR. Rental is allowed for a period of continuous use not to exceed 13 months. The two-month rental trial period does not count towards the 13-month rental period. After the two-month rental trial period, the TENS unit is considered purchased in the month in which the total of all amounts allowed, for one or multiple charges, reaches the applicable purchase amount or exceeds the 13-month rental period.

If the TENS unit is approved for on-going use, and the unit is purchased, the supplier must submit the charge with the appropriate purchase modifier. The amount allowed is either the new equipment purchase rate or used equipment purchase rate, as described in the General Policy Guidelines section of this policy, for the month billed. If the item was previously rented, then the purchase rate is based on the purchase rate in effect at the time of the first month's rental. The two-month rental trial period does not count towards the purchase amount. After the two-month rental trial period, the TENS unit is considered purchased in the month in which the total of all amounts allowed, for one or multiple charges, reaches the applicable purchase amount or exceeds the 13-month rental period. Specific Guidelines for DME Items Categorized as Inexpensive or Routinely Purchased (IRP) DME Items Although transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulator (TENS) units qualify as items of IRP DME, reimbursement for TENS units differs. See the Transcutaneous Electrical Nerve Stimulator section of this policy. Humana requires an appropriate transaction modifier. Humana determines the amount allowed based on the transaction modifier billed for an item categorized as IRP DME as described below.

If a charge for a covered IRP DME item is submitted with modifier RR, the amount allowed is the monthly rental rate. However, Humana reserves the right to allow at the purchase rate at any time, regardless of the submission of modifier RR. An IRP DME item is considered purchased in the month in which the total of all amounts allowed equals the applicable purchase amount for that item.

To indicate that a charge is for the purchase of an IRP DME item, the supplier must submit the charge with the appropriate purchase modifier. The amount allowed is either the new equipment purchase rate or used equipment purchase rate, as described in the

General Policy Guidelines section of this policy, for the month billed. If the item was previously rented, then the purchase rate is based on the purchase rate in effect at the time of the first month's rental, less the total amount allowed for all previous rentals.

Humana may reimburse the replacement of a DME base item, part or accessory after the expiration of the RUL if it is still medically necessary but no longer functional. The RUL period begins the first date of service when the specific base item, part or accessory was individually reimbursed. Additionally, the following criteria must be met:

The maximum number of allowed units has not been exceeded.

The cost to replace a part or accessory, including labor and parts, does not exceed the cost of renting or purchasing a new base item.

Base item, part or accessory replacement is not due to intentional damage, neglect or misuse of equipment.

Replacement of a part or accessory is only allowed for a member if the same member owns the base item.

The base item, part or accessory must not be under warranty. Documentation of an expired or denied warranty is required, upon request.

The base item, part or accessory is not currently being rented.

In addition to the relevant requirements outlined above, the following conditions apply to replacement of a DME base item, part or accessory before expiration of the RUL.

Humana may reimburse the replacement of a base item, part or accessory before expiration of the RUL only if either of the following scenarios are true:

The member's medical needs have changed such that a different item is medically necessary; or

The item was lost, stolen or unintentionally damaged beyond repair. For only the first charge for the replacement item, modifier RA must be billed with the Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System (HCPCS) code for a base item, part or accessory replaced for one of the scenarios described above.

Humana may reimburse the replacement of a part or accessory in association with the covered repair of a base item before the expiration of the RUL of the part or accessory when the following criteria are met:

The part or accessory is not an upgrade to the base item.

Replacement is necessary to make the base item functional.

The part or accessory is not billed on the same date of service as the base item.

The base item is not categorized as Frequently Serviced or Oxygen Equipment.

A charge for the base item was not previously denied.

The base item was previously purchased, including an item for which payment has capped through rental payments.

Modifier RR is not also billed.

Box 19 on the claim form or its electronic equivalent includes the base item code and purchase date. Modifier RB must be billed with the HCPCS code for that replaced part or accessory. When all requirements are met, the replacement of a part or accessory will be allowed at the purchase rate.

Humana's Making it Easier web-based training series includes a video highlighting Humana's guidance on durable medical equipment that may supplement your understanding of this policy.

Capped rental modifier: A modifier that indicates the rental month. Modifier KH indicates a charge for the initial month supplied. Modifier KI indicates a charge for the second or third month supplied. Modifier KJ indicates a charge for the fourth or later month supplied.

Medicare Durable Medical Equipment, Prosthetics, Orthotics and Supplies (DMEPOS) Fee Schedule: A file published by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) that includes, among other information, codes that indicate the CMS-defined DMEPOS categories for DMEPOS items.

Transaction modifier: A modifier that indicates whether the charge is for rental of the item or purchase of the item; and, if for purchase, whether the item was new or used. The transaction modifiers described in this policy are modifiers NU, RR and UE.

Purchase modifier: A modifier that indicates whether the charge is for the purchase of new equipment or used equipment. The purchase modifiers described in this policy are modifiers NU and UE.

The following modifiers may be used when billing DME items. This is not an all-inclusive list.

Modifier KH: DMEPOS item, initial claim, purchase or first month rental

Modifier KJ: DMEPOS, parenteral and enteral nutrition (PEN) pump or capped rental, months four to fifteen

Modifier MS: Six month maintenance and servicing fee for reasonable and necessary parts and labor which are not covered under any manufacturer or supplier warranty

Modifier QA: Prescribed amounts of stationary oxygen for daytime use while at rest and nighttime use differ and the average of the two amounts is less than 1 liter per minute (LPM)

Modifier QB: Prescribed amounts of stationary oxygen for daytime use while at rest and nighttime use differ and the average of the two amounts exceeds 4 liters per minute (LPM) and portable oxygen is prescribed

Modifier QE: Prescribed amount of stationary oxygen while at rest is less than 1 liter per minute (LPM)

Modifier QF: Prescribed amount of stationary oxygen while at rest exceeds 4 liters per minute (LPM) and portable oxygen is prescribed

Modifier QG: Prescribed amount of stationary oxygen while at rest is greater than 4 liters per minute (LPM)

Modifier QR: Prescribed amounts of stationary oxygen for daytime use while at rest and nighttime use differ and the average of the two amounts is greater than 4 liters per minute (LPM)

Modifier RB: Replacement of a part of DME, orthotic or prosthetic item furnished as part of a repair

definitions.content:

Medicare Durable Medical Equipment, Prosthetics, Orthotics and Supplies (DMEPOS) Fee Schedule: A file published by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) that includes, among other information, codes that indicate the CMS-defined DMEPOS categories for DMEPOS items.

Transaction modifier: A modifier that indicates whether the charge is for rental of the item or purchase of the item; and, if for purchase, whether the item was new or used. The transaction modifiers described in this policy are modifiers NU, RR and UE.

Purchase modifier: A modifier that indicates whether the charge is for the purchase of new equipment or used equipment. The purchase modifiers described in this policy are modifiers NU and UE.

extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Overview
extracted_content.content: Consistent with healthcare industry standards, Humana expects suppliers of durable medical equipment, prosthetics, orthotics and supplies (DMEPOS) to retain proof of delivery (POD) documentation in their files and make it available to Humana upon request. Maintaining POD documentation is one of the supplier standards for DMEPOS suppliers participating in the Medicare Program as noted in the Code of Federal Regulations.

extracted_content.title: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: In addition to this policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. Humana requires DMEPOS suppliers to maintain complete and accurate POD documentation, consistent with the standards of chapter 4, section 4.7.3.1 and chapter 5, section 5.10 of the Medicare Program Integrity Manual. Humana requires suppliers to make POD documentation available to Humana upon request. A Humana plan denies a charge for a service that lacks appropriate supplier POD documentation and requires reimbursement of any overpayment.
