extracted_content.title: Overview
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Overview
extracted_content.content: The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) has directed providers to use modifier CT to report computed tomography (CT) services furnished on equipment that is not consistent with dose optimization standards established by the National Electrical Manufacturers Association (NEMA). Enforcement of NEMA Standard XR 29-2013, also known as the MITA Smart Dose standard, for the Medicare Program is required by the Protecting Access to Medicare Act of 2014. The criteria of NEMA Standard XR 29-2013 ensure use of the lowest radiation dose necessary to get the image quality needed by providers to make a proper diagnosis. The standard outlines four attributes CT equipment should meet to ensure that a patient receives the highest standard of care as established by professional societies and regulatory agencies. Performing CT services on equipment that meets all elements of the standard helps reduce a patient's lifetime exposure to potentially cancer-causing medical radiation. Humana works to reduce our members' exposure to medical radiation. Directly and through vendor partnerships, we educate our members on the risks of medical radiation exposure and encourage our in-network providers to provide high quality advanced diagnostic services that meet a broad set of industry standards, including NEMA Standard XR 29-2013. This policy outlines Humana's billing requirements and reimbursement for services reported with modifier CT.

Humana requires providers to follow the appropriate Medicare Program guidance for correct coding using modifier CT. Providers must report modifier CT with procedure codes for applicable CT services performed on equipment that does not meet all four attributes of NEMA Standard XR 29-2013. Humana reduces reimbursement for the technical component (TC) of an applicable CT service reported with modifier CT by five percent for dates of service in 2016 and by 15 percent for dates of service beginning January 1, 2017. Note: Pre-authorization requirements may apply when applicable CT services are provided to a Humana member.

reimbursement_guidelines.title: Reimbursement Guidelines
reimbursement_guidelines.content:
In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. Humana requires providers to follow the appropriate Medicare Program guidance for correct coding using modifier CT. Providers must report modifier CT with procedure codes for applicable CT services performed on equipment that does not meet all four attributes of NEMA Standard XR 29-2013. Humana reduces reimbursement for the technical component (TC) of an applicable CT service reported with modifier CT by five percent for dates of service in 2016 and by 15 percent for dates of service beginning January 1, 2017. Note: Pre-authorization requirements may apply when applicable CT services are provided to a Humana member.

Modifier CT: Computed tomography services furnished using equipment that does not meet each of the attributes of the National Electrical Manufacturers Association (NEMA) XR-29-2013 standard.

Technical component (TC): The technical component of a service is for all non-physician work and includes administrative, personnel and capital (equipment and facility) costs and related malpractice expenses. Modifier TC is used with the billing code to indicate that the TC is being billed.

extracted_content.title: Overview
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Overview
extracted_content.content: The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) has directed providers to use modifier FX to report X-ray services furnished using film. Effective for dates of service beginning January 1, 2017, Original Medicare reimbursement for the technical component (TC) of film X-ray services reported with modifier FX is reduced by 20 percent. The film X-ray reimbursement reduction is required for the Medicare Program by the Consolidated Appropriations Act of 2016. Transitioning from film X-ray technology to digital radiography (DR) technology ensures use of the lowest radiation dose necessary to get the image quality needed by providers to make a proper diagnosis. Performing X-rays using DR technology ensures that a patient receives the highest standard of care as established by professional societies and regulatory agencies and helps reduce a patient's lifetime exposure to potentially cancer-causing medical radiation. Humana works to reduce our members' exposure to medical radiation. Directly and through vendor partnerships, we educate our members on the risks of medical radiation exposure and encourage our in-network providers to provide high quality advanced diagnostic services that meet a broad set of industry standards.

extracted_content.title: Overview
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Overview
extracted_content.content: The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) global surgical policy states that reimbursement for a procedure that has a global surgical package includes payment for preoperative, intraoperative and postoperative care, as well as payment for various related services, such as complications following surgery, postsurgical pain management and supplies. There are occasions when more than one qualified healthcare practitioner provides services included in the global surgical package of a surgery. For example, the physician who performs the surgical procedure may not provide the follow-up care. In such situations, for a global surgical package that may be split, it is appropriate to reimburse the various practitioners for portions of the global surgical package. For a surgery with a global surgical package, a practitioner indicates the portion of the global surgical package performed by using modifiers 54, 55 and 56, as appropriate. This policy outlines Humana's billing requirements and reimbursement for a service reported with modifier 54, 55 or 56.

extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: In addition to this policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. This policy applies to global surgery procedure codes as identified on the Medicare Physician Fee Schedule (MPFS) Relative Value File and applies to professional services only.

extracted_content.title: Billing Requirements
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Billing Requirements
extracted_content.content: Humana requires practitioners to report modifiers 54, 55 and 56 according to applicable guidance published by CMS. This includes, but is not limited to, the CMS requirement to report modifier 54 when the practitioner furnishes the intraoperative care only regardless of whether there has been a formal transfer or care. In the absence of applicable CMS guidance, the practitioner should report modifiers 54, 55 and 55 according to the guidance described below.

extracted_content.title: Reimbursement
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Billing Requirements > Reimbursement
extracted_content.content: Humana plans determine the amount allowed for a segment of split global care for a service with a global surgery period as outlined below.

extracted_content.title: Modifier 54
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Billing Requirements > Modifier 54
extracted_content.content: Humana considers a charge submitted with modifier 54 as a charge for both preoperative management and intraoperative care, unless there is a coverable charge for the same procedure code for preoperative management only, as indicated by modifier 56. If there is a coverable charge submitted with modifier 56 for the same service, the plan considers a charge submitted with modifier 54 as a charge for intraoperative care only. Humana allows a charge for intraoperative care only, indicated by modifier 54, at the contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member's plan for the service multiplied by that service's MPFS intraoperative percentage. Humana allows a charge for both preoperative management and intraoperative care, indicated by modifier 54, as the sum of the contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member's plan for the service multiplied by that service's MPFS preoperative percentage and the contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member's plan for the service multiplied by that service's MPFS intraoperative percentage.

extracted_content.title: Modifier 55
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Billing Requirements > Modifier 55
extracted_content.content: Humana allows a charge for postoperative management only, as indicated by modifier 55, at the contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member's plan for the service, multiplied by that service's MPFS postoperative percentage, and multiplied by the percentage of the global surgery period for which the billing practitioner provided care. Effectively, the total of all percentages of a global surgery period for which practitioners were responsible for postoperative management is 100%. Therefore, the plan does not allow more than 100% of the postoperative management for that service. Humana expects a practitioner to report, in the units field on the claim form, the number of days of service that the practitioner provided, consistent with the transfer of postoperative management to which the practitioners agreed.

extracted_content.title: Modifier 56
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Billing Requirements > Modifier 56
extracted_content.content: Humana allows a charge for preoperative management only, indicated by modifier 56, at the contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member's plan for the service multiplied by that service's MPFS preoperative percentage.

reimbursement_guidelines.content: Humana plans determine the amount allowed for a segment of split global care for a service with a global surgery period as outlined below.

definitions.title: Definitions
definitions.content:
Base maximum amount payable under the member's plan: The maximum amount of reimbursement for a covered expense, determined by the member's plan. Depending on the plan, this may be the maximum allowable fee, the appropriate Medicare fee schedule rate or an amount derived from another payment model. Actual plan reimbursement may be less than this base maximum amount, because of applicable adjustments.

Global surgery period(s): The number of days that constitute preoperative management, intraoperative care and postoperative management.

- Zero-day minor surgery or procedure: Day of surgery only for a total global period of one day.

- 10-day minor surgery or procedure: Zero preoperative management days, day of surgery and 10 postoperative management

days for a total global period of 11 days.

- 90-day major surgery or procedure: One preoperative management day, day of surgery and 90 postoperative management

days for a total global period of 92 days.

Global surgical package: All services for which reimbursement would be included in a global surgery payment; services that would be separately reimbursable are not part of the global surgical package.

Intraoperative care: For a service with a global surgery period, the surgical care, including postoperative care before discharge from the facility.

Medicare Physician Fee Schedule (MPFS) Relative Value File: A file published by CMS that includes, among other information, percentages of the global surgical package for the preoperative, intraoperative and postoperative management of a patient; and the professional procedure relative value unit (RVU).

Modifier 54: Surgical care only.

Modifier 55: Postoperative management only.

Modifier 56: Preoperative management only.

Preoperative management: For a service with a global surgery period, that portion of a global surgical package provided before the surgical care.

Postoperative management: For a service with a global surgery period, that portion of a global surgical package provided after the surgical care and after discharge from the facility.

Split global care: Global surgical package services provided, under a transfer of care, by multiple qualified healthcare practitioners.

Base unit: For billing purposes, the specific amount of a drug that is defined in the unit measurement indicated in the drug code's long descriptor. Example: If the drug code's long descriptor defines the code as "10 mg", one base unit for that code is 10 milligrams.

Efficient administration amount: The total amount for the vials or packages that, in combination, represent the minimum amount necessary for use, given all the vial or package sizes available for provider purchase, to administer the appropriate amount.

Modifier JW: Drug amount discarded/not administered to any patient.

Modifier JZ: Zero drug amount discarded/not administered to any patient.

extracted_content.content: This policy outlines Humana's billing expectations for reporting Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System (HCPCS) modifiers XE, XP, XS and XU, known collectively as modifiers X{EPSU}.

extracted_content.title: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. Each one of the modifiers X{EPSU} defines a unique subset of distinct procedural services. Modifier 59 is used to report distinct procedural services more generally without the specificity provided by modifiers X{EPSU}. Current Procedural Terminology (CPT®) instructions from the American Medical Association (AMA) state that modifier 59 should not be used if a more descriptive modifier is available to report the special circumstances. When one of the modifiers X{EPSU} more accurately describes the circumstances of a distinct procedural service than modifier 59, Humana encourages the reporting of that modifier, instead of modifier 59. Modifiers X{EPSU} should not be appended to evaluation and management (E/M) services.

reimbursement_guidelines.title: Reimbursement Guidelines
reimbursement_guidelines.content:
In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. Each one of the modifiers X{EPSU} defines a unique subset of distinct procedural services. Modifier 59 is used to report distinct procedural services more generally without the specificity provided by modifiers X{EPSU}. Current Procedural Terminology (CPT®) instructions from the American Medical Association (AMA) state that modifier 59 should not be used if a more descriptive modifier is available to report the special circumstances. When one of the modifiers X{EPSU} more accurately describes the circumstances of a distinct procedural service than modifier 59, Humana encourages the reporting of that modifier, instead of modifier 59. Modifiers X{EPSU} should not be appended to evaluation and management (E/M) services.

Humana's Making it Easier web-based training series includes a video on the proper reporting of modifiers 59 and X{EPSU} that may supplement your understanding of this policy.

Modifier 59: Distinct procedural service.

Modifier XE: Separate encounter.

Modifier XP: Separate practitioner.

Modifier XS: Separate structure.

Modifier XU: Unusual non-overlapping service.

Modifiers X{EPSU}: Modifiers XE, XP, XS and XU, collectively.

extracted_content.title: Overview
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Overview
extracted_content.content: This policy outlines various multiple procedure payment reductions (MPPR). Practitioner reimbursement for a procedure code generally includes reimbursement for the individual costs, also known as inputs, typically associated with that service. For example, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) uses a formula that accounts for the inputs associated with a procedure code to determine Medicare Physician Fee Schedule (MPFS) reimbursement rates for that code. When the same provider renders multiple services, or multiple units of the same service, to the same patient on the same day, the total calculation for the procedure code(s) could account more than once for an input that was only rendered once. Examples of inputs that might be contemplated in reimbursement for certain procedure codes, that would not typically be duplicated in the same encounter include: greeting and gowning the patient; preparing the room, equipment and supplies; providing education and obtaining consent. An MPPR adjusts reimbursement to offset duplication of reimbursement for inputs that were only rendered once.

extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Special Rules for Endoscopic Services
extracted_content.content: For an endoscopic service, multiple endoscopy reduction and multiple surgery reduction are determined separately. This will result in one of the following scenarios, depending on the number of services billed and the individual multiple procedure indicator code of each service:

extracted_content.title: Special Rules for Endoscopic Services
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Special Rules for Endoscopic Services
extracted_content.content: Multiple endoscopy reduction alone could apply to the service.

extracted_content.title: Special Rules for Endoscopic Services
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Special Rules for Endoscopic Services
extracted_content.content: Multiple surgery reduction alone could apply to the service.

extracted_content.title: Special Rules for Endoscopic Services
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Special Rules for Endoscopic Services
extracted_content.content: Both multiple endoscopy reduction and multiple surgery reduction could apply to the service.

extracted_content.title: Special Rules for Endoscopic Services
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Special Rules for Endoscopic Services
extracted_content.content: Neither multiple endoscopy reduction nor multiple surgery reduction could apply to the service. If multiple endoscopy reduction applies, it is always determined before multiple surgery reduction. After determining any multiple endoscopy reductions, all endoscopic services in the same endoscopic family are treated as a single service for the purpose of determining multiple surgery reduction, as follows:

extracted_content.title: Special Rules for Endoscopic Services
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Special Rules for Endoscopic Services
extracted_content.content: For multiple surgery reduction ranking purposes, endoscopic procedures in the same endoscopic family are treated as one service.

extracted_content.title: Special Rules for Endoscopic Services
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Special Rules for Endoscopic Services
extracted_content.content: An endoscopic family's multiple surgery reduction ranking establishes the multiple surgery reduction percentage, if any, for all services in that endoscopic family. Note: Additional payment rules may apply in certain circumstances. For example, when a bilateral adjustment is applicable, it will be applied before a multiple surgery reduction.

reimbursement_guidelines.content:

In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements.

For diagnostic cardiovascular services, the portion of an in-network practitioner's contracted rate that is attributable to the technical component (TC) may be subject to MPPR. For diagnostic cardiovascular services rendered by an out-of-network practitioner, the portion of the base maximum amount payable under the member's plan that is attributable to the TC may be subject to MPPR. For reimbursement of only a TC, all of the contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member's plan is attributable to the TC. For reimbursement of both a TC and a professional component (PC), the portion of the contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member's plan that is attributable to the TC is that rate or amount multiplied by the ratio of the code's MPFS local TC amount to the code's MPFS local global amount. For example:

ccccc $10 $16 $20 16 20 = 80% $10 x 80% = $8 Humana applies an MPPR to same-day diagnostic cardiovascular TC services rendered by the same provider. To determine whether the MPPR applies to a specific allowed charge or to one or more units of a charge with multiple allowed units: First, of the services for which Humana is reimbursing for a TC, Humana identifies the same-day services with a MPFS Relative Value File multiple procedure indicator 6. Second, Humana ranks all identified services from highest dollar amount to lowest dollar amount. We rank by the portion of the charge's per-unit practitioner's contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member's plan that is attributable to TC, as described above.

When Humana determines to apply diagnostic cardiovascular services TC MPPR to a unit, a 25 percent reduction is applied to the reimbursement for the portion of the unit's practitioner's contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member's plan that is attributable to TC.

When Humana determines to apply diagnostic imaging services TC MPPR to a unit, a 50 percent reduction is applied to the reimbursement for the portion of the unit's practitioner's contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member's plan that is attributable to TC. Note: In certain circumstances, additional payment rules may apply.

For diagnostic imaging services, the portion of an in-network practitioner's contracted rate that is attributable to the PC may be amount payable under the member's plan that is attributable to the PC may be subject to MPPR. For reimbursement of both a PC and a TC, the portion of the contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member's plan that is attributable to the PC is that rate or amount multiplied by the ratio of the code's MPFS local PC amount to the code's MPFS local global amount. Humana applies an MPPR to same-day diagnostic imaging PC services rendered by the same provider.

We rank by the portion of the charge's per-unit practitioner's contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member's plan that is attributable to PC, as described above. Finally, Humana eliminates from review the unit of service that is ranked highest; or, if multiple units of service are ranked highest, Humana eliminates one of those units. Humana applies MPPR to all other allowed units of service. When Humana determines to apply diagnostic imaging services PC MPPR to a unit:

For dates of service on or after January 1, 2017, a 5 percent reduction is applied to the reimbursement for the portion of the unit's practitioner's contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member's plan that is attributable to PC.

For dates of service before January 1, 2017, a 25 percent reduction is applied to the reimbursement for the portion of the unit's practitioner's contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member's plan that is attributable to PC. Always Therapy: A service that is always considered a therapy, as noted in the Medicare Physician Fee Schedule (MPFS) Relative Value File by a multiple procedure indicator 5.

Base maximum amount payable under the member's plan: The maximum amount of reimbursement for a unit of a covered expense, determined by the member's plan. Depending on the plan, this may be the maximum allowable fee, the appropriate Medicare fee schedule rate or an amount derived from another payment model. Actual plan reimbursement may be less than this base maximum amount, because of applicable adjustments.

Medicare Physician Fee Schedule (MPFS) Relative Value File: A file published by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services that includes, among other information, multiple procedure indicator, relative value units and conversion factors for practitioner services. This file is commonly referred to as the relative value unit (RVU) table. Elements of the file that are referenced in this policy include the following:

CF: The conversion factor is the amount shown in the MPFS Relative Value File for the appropriate year.

PE GPCI: The practice expense geographic price index for the area where the service was rendered, shown in the MPFS Relative Value File for the appropriate year.

PE RVU: The practice expense relative value unit is the amount shown in the MPFS Relative Value File for the appropriate year.

Modifier 26: Professional component.

Modifier 51: Multiple procedures.

Modifier 59: Distinct procedural service.

Modifier TC: Technical component.

Modifiers X{EPSU}: Modifiers XE, XP, XS and XU, collectively.

Modifier XE: Separate encounter.

Modifier XP: Separate practitioner.

Modifier XS: Separate structure.

Modifier XU: Unusual non-overlapping service.

Practice Expense (PE): One of three groups of inputs used to determine pricing of services covered under the Medicare Physician Fee Schedule (MPFS); PE accounts for costs of running a practice (other than expenses associated with professional liability and the practitioner's actual work), including rent, equipment, supplies and staff costs other than the work performed by the practitioner personally.

Professional Component (PC): The professional component of a service is for practitioner work interpreting a diagnostic test or performing a procedure and includes indirect practice and malpractice expenses related to that work.

Same Provider: A single qualified practitioner or multiple practitioners within the same group practice.

Technical Component (TC): The technical component of a service is for all non-practitioner work and includes administrative, personnel and capital (equipment and facility) costs and related malpractice expenses.

extracted_content.title: Overview
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Overview
extracted_content.content: Section 1833(q) of the Social Security Act requires charges for some Medicare Program services to be submitted with ordering or referring provider information from a qualified healthcare provider. This requirement ensures quality of care because many services require a qualified healthcare provider to interpret and provide guidance to the patient. Supplying a valid National Provider Identifier (NPI) of the ordering or referring qualified healthcare provider helps in the verification that services rendered were necessary and medically reviewed and that follow-up care is available. Original Medicare began rejecting claims without valid ordering or referring provider information January 6, 2014.

reimbursement_guidelines.title: Reimbursement Guidelines
reimbursement_guidelines.content:
In addition to this policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements.

Humana plans require valid orders for the same types of services for which Original Medicare requires orders and require valid referrals for the same types of services for which Original Medicare requires referrals. To be valid, an order or referral must have been issued by a qualified healthcare provider. The services of a Part A home health agency, specifically, may only be ordered or referred by a doctor of medicine, doctor of osteopathy or doctor of podiatry. Humana plans deny charges for services for which Humana requires valid orders or referrals when those services were provided in the absence of an applicable, valid order or referral; when appropriate, plans require reimbursement of overpayments.

Humana requires providers to maintain complete and accurate documentation of orders and referrals for services for which Humana requires orders and referrals. Humana requires providers to make order and referral documentation available to Humana upon request. Humana plans deny charges for services that lack appropriate order or referral documentation; when appropriate, plans require reimbursement of overpayments.

A charge for a service that requires a valid order or referral must be submitted with the name and NPI of the ordering or referring provider, that provider must be a qualified healthcare provider, and that provider's name and NPI must be accurate and valid. Humana plans deny charges for services that require orders or referrals if those charges are not submitted as described herein; when appropriate, plans require reimbursement of overpayments.

The following are examples of services that require ordering or referring provider information as described above. This is not an all- inclusive list.

Durable medical equipment, prosthetics, orthotics and supplies (DMEPOS)

Humana expects providers to follow the respective state Medicaid agency ordering and referring provider requirements. Humana Medicaid plans allow charges for services consistent with state Medicaid guidelines regarding ordering and referring provider requirements.

Applicable: An order or referral is applicable to rendered services when those services were provided pursuant to that order or referral.

Overpayments: Amounts paid to the provider for services that lack documentation.

Qualified healthcare provider: As used herein, means an individual licensed as one of the following: dental surgeon, doctor of medicine, doctor of osteopathy, doctor of dental medicine, doctor of podiatry, optometrist (may only order DME, laboratory and X-ray services), nurse practitioner, physician assistant, certified clinical nurse specialist, clinical psychologist, intern, resident, fellow, certified nurse midwife and clinical social worker.

Refer/referral: As used herein, means the process of a qualified healthcare provider directing work to another provider. This is also known as "certifying." It is thus distinct from the way that term might be used in any other contexts to describe the process established by the health plan to authorize outpatient specialty care services or inpatient services not rendered by the member's primary care physician.

extracted_content.content: Facility billing guidelines for the UB-04 claim form, also known as the CMS-1450, and the 837 institutional electronic equivalent require providers to bill revenue codes to describe services furnished. extracted_content.content: Pass-through billing occurs when a provider bills for a service for which neither that provider nor any individual under that provider's direct employment performed that service. extracted_content.content: Pass-through billing is generally prohibited, with limited exceptions, for Medicare Advantage basic benefits (i.e., benefits that would be covered under Original Medicare Parts A and B). A provider may not bill, charge, seek payment or have any recourse against Humana or any Humana Medicare Advantage member for any amounts related to a denied pass-through billed service for basic benefits.

extracted_content.title: Limited Exceptions
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Limited Exceptions
extracted_content.content: The following are limited exceptions to the general prohibition against pass-through billing. A provider may submit a charge for potentially covered services rendered by another qualified provider under only the following circumstances. In all of these circumstances, the submitting provider may not bill an amount greater than the amount the submitting provider paid or will pay the rendering provider for the service. Humana will not pay any amount greater than the amount the submitting provider pays the rendering provider for the service. The billing provider must make available to Humana documentation of the amount paid to the rendering provider.

extracted_content.title: Purchased diagnostic or screening tests exception
extracted_content.subsection: Purchased diagnostic or screening tests exception
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Purchased diagnostic or screening tests exception
extracted_content.content: Note: This section does not apply to clinical diagnostic laboratory tests paid by Original Medicare under the Clinical Laboratory Fee Schedule. A physician or other professional may bill for the technical component (TC) and/or professional component (PC) of a diagnostic test that was ordered by the physician or other professional, or ordered by a party related to the billing physician or other supplier through common ownership or control. However, anti-markup payment limitations apply if the diagnostic test is performed by a physician who does not "share a practice" with the billing physician or other professional. The performing provider for the TC is the professional who conducted or supervised the test, and the performing provider for the PC is the professional who interpreted the results. Under anti-markup payment limitations, payment to the billing physician or other professional, minus beneficiary cost-sharing, for the TC or PC of the diagnostic test may not exceed the lowest of the following amounts:

extracted_content.content: If the performing physician is deemed to "share a practice" with the billing physician or other professional who ordered the test, the anti-markup payment limitation does not apply. extracted_content.title: Exception to the anti-markup payment limitation

extracted_content.content: The performing physician provides "substantially all" (at least 75 percent) of his or her professional services through the billing physician or other professional, as discussed below; or

extracted_content.title: Exception to the anti-markup payment limitation

extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Exception to the anti-markup payment limitation
extracted_content.content: The services were performed under a "site of service/same building" arrangement as discussed below. The "substantially all" services requirement will be satisfied if, at the time the billing physician or other professional submits a claim for a service provided by the performing physician, the billing physician or other professional has a reasonable belief that:

extracted_content.title: Exception to the anti-markup payment limitation
extracted_content.subsection: Exception to the anti-markup payment limitation
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Exception to the anti-markup payment limitation
extracted_content.content: For the 12 months prior to and including the month in which the service was performed, the performing physician provided substantially all of his or her professional services through the billing physician or other professional; or

extracted_content.title: Exception to the anti-markup payment limitation
extracted_content.subsection: Exception to the anti-markup payment limitation
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Exception to the anti-markup payment limitation
extracted_content.content: The performing physician will provide substantially all of his or her professional services through the billing physician or other professional for the next 12 months (including the month in which the service is performed). The performing physician may be deemed to "share a practice" with the billing physician or other professional if the services were performed under a "site of service/same building" arrangement. This alternative approach requires the performing physician to be an owner, employer or independent contractor of the billing physician or other professional and requires that the TC or PC be performed in the "office of the billing physician or other supplier." The "office of the billing physician or other supplier" is any medical office space, regardless of the number of locations, in which the ordering physician or other professional regularly provides patient care. It also includes space where the billing physician or other supplier furnishes diagnostic testing services, if the space is located in the "same building" in which the ordering physician or other ordering professional regularly provides patient care. With respect to a billing physician or other professional that is a "physician organization," the "office of the billing physician or other supplier" is space in which the ordering physician provides substantially the full range of patient care services the ordering physician provides generally. "Same building" and "physician organization" are defined in 42 CFR §411.351. The billing physician or other professional must keep on file the performing physician's name, address and the National Provider Identifier. The physician or other professional providing the TC or PC of the diagnostic test must be enrolled in the Medicare Program. No formal reassignment is necessary.

extracted_content.content: A charge submitted by a Social Security Act Section 1861(u) "provider of services," for a service rendered by another provider that, under Original Medicare, would be payable to the Section 1861(u) "provider of services." A "provider of services" includes a hospital, critical access hospital, skilled nursing facility, comprehensive outpatient rehabilitation facility, home health agency, hospice program or, for certain purposes, a fund.

extracted_content.title: General Readmission Review Requirements
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: References > General Readmission Review Requirements
extracted_content.content: All readmissions, to the same facility, reimbursed using Diagnosis Related Group (DRG) methodology are subject to review to determine if the readmission was preventable.

extracted_content.title: Preventable Readmissions
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: References > Preventable Readmissions
extracted_content.content: If Humana determines that a readmission was preventable, Humana does not allow payment for the second admission since reimbursement for the first admission includes reimbursement for the second admission. The following are examples of preventable readmissions. This is not an all-inclusive list:

extracted_content.title: Preventable Readmissions
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: References > Preventable Readmissions
extracted_content.content: Premature discharge that resulted in a readmission. This is based on information that the provider or physician knew, or should have known, at the time of discharge.

extracted_content.title: Preventable Readmissions
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: References > Preventable Readmissions
extracted_content.content: Care rendered during the second admission that should have occurred during the first admission.

extracted_content.title: Preventable Readmissions
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: References > Preventable Readmissions
extracted_content.content: An inappropriate transfer.

extracted_content.title: Preventable Readmissions
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: References > Preventable Readmissions
extracted_content.content: A readmission that was not medically necessary.

extracted_content.title: Preventable Readmissions
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: References > Preventable Readmissions
extracted_content.content: A readmission that is an attempt to circumvent Inpatient Prospective Payment System (IPPS) payment.

extracted_content.title: Separately Payable Admissions
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: References > Separately Payable Admissions
extracted_content.content: If Humana determines that a subsequent admission was not preventable or was unrelated to the prior admission, Humana may allow separate payment for each admission. The following are examples of admissions that may be separately payable:

extracted_content.title: Separately Payable Admissions
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: References > Separately Payable Admissions
extracted_content.content: An admission that is due to a reoccurrence of a chronic condition and is not a continuation of the previous episode's admission.

extracted_content.title: Separately Payable Admissions
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: References > Separately Payable Admissions
extracted_content.content: An unrelated readmission, including an unrelated same-day readmission. Facilities cannot be held responsible for readmissions beyond their control, which may include, but are not limited to, the following:

extracted_content.title: Separately Payable Admissions
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: References > Separately Payable Admissions
extracted_content.content: Failure of the patient to follow discharge instructions. This requires documentation that instructions were properly communicated to a patient or caregiver who was both not impaired and capable of following the instructions.

extracted_content.content: A readmission after the patient left the same facility against medical advice.

reimbursement_guidelines.title: Reimbursement Guidelines
reimbursement_guidelines.content:
In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. The following policy applies to facility services only.

Observation stays following an inpatient admission at the same facility are subject to review to determine if the subsequent observation stay was preventable.

If Humana determines that a subsequent observation stay was preventable, Humana does not allow payment for the subsequent observation stay. The following are examples of preventable subsequent observation stays. This is not an all-inclusive list:

Premature discharge from an inpatient admission that resulted in a subsequent observation stay. This is based on information that the provider or physician knew, or should have known, at the time of discharge.

Care rendered during the subsequent observation stay that should have occurred during the prior inpatient admission.

A subsequent observation stay that was not medically necessary.

A subsequent observation stay that is an attempt to circumvent Inpatient Prospective Payment System (IPPS) payment.

If Humana determines that a subsequent observation stay was not preventable or was unrelated to the prior admission, Humana may allow separate payment for both the prior inpatient admission and the subsequent observation stay. The following are examples of subsequent observation stays that may be separately payable:

A subsequent observation stay that is due to a reoccurrence of a chronic condition and is not a continuation of the previous episode's prior inpatient admission.

An unrelated subsequent observation stay, including an unrelated same-day subsequent observation stay. Facilities cannot be held responsible for subsequent observation stays beyond their control, which may include, but are not limited to, the following:

Failure of the patient to follow discharge instructions. This requires documentation that instructions were properly communicated to a patient or caregiver who was both not impaired and capable of following the instructions.

A condition caused by post-care services provided beyond the facility's control.

A subsequent observation stay after the patient left the same facility against medical advice.

Same facility: An entity that owns or controls the facility for the prior inpatient admission, an entity owned or controlled by the facility for the prior inpatient admission, or an entity that is under common ownership or control as the facility for the prior inpatient admission.

Subsequent observation stay: A hospital stay during which the patient is placed in observation status, but not admitted as an inpatient, that follows a prior inpatient admission.

extracted_content.title: Sessions and Fractions
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Sessions and Fractions
extracted_content.content: CPT code 77427 may only be submitted for five sessions, regardless of the actual time period in which the services were furnished. Multiple fractions representing two or more treatment sessions furnished on the same day may be counted separately only if there was a distinct break between same-day therapy sessions, and only if the fractions are of a character usually furnished on different days. Humana plans deny, as inappropriately billed, charges for fewer than five sessions. Exception: A provider may submit CPT code 77427 for three or four sessions at the end of a course of treatment. Humana plans deny, as inappropriately billed, charges at the end of a course of treatment for fewer than three sessions.

extracted_content.title: Units
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Units
extracted_content.content: The billing provider must submit each unit of five sessions as a distinct single-unit charge. For a three-session unit or four-session unit at the end of a course of treatment, the billing provider must submit a single-unit charge distinct from all other units. Humana plans allow no more than one unit per charge and deny any additional unit(s) as inappropriately billed.

extracted_content.content: Humana plans require providers to submit each charge for CPT code 77427 with a "from" date representing the date of the first session of the charge and a "to" date representing the date of the last session of the charge.

extracted_content.title: Note
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Note
extracted_content.content: A provider must submit a charge for CPT code 77427 with a note indicating the number of fractions performed. Use the following syntax in Loop 2400 in the 837 electronic transaction: "NTE✽ADD✽X FRACTION(S)~". For example, if five fractions were performed, enter "NTE✽ADD✽5 FRACTIONS~". If one fraction was performed, enter "NTE✽ADD✽1 FRACTION~".

reimbursement_guidelines.title: Reimbursement Guidelines
reimbursement_guidelines.content:
In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. To make a correction to data that was in any type of previous provider submission, whether a reimbursable claim or a non- reimbursable encounter for which information is gathered for reporting, including a correction that adds entirely new data, such as late charges, Humana requires a provider to:

Submit a complete replacement of the claim submitted previously.

In that replacement claim, report a claim frequency code of 7 to indicate that it is a replacement claim, as follows:

In loop 2300 CLM05-3 of an 837 electronic transaction;

In the resubmission code field in box 22 of a CMS-1500 paper claim form; or

As the final digit of the type of bill (TOB) code in box 4 of a UB-04, also known as a CMS-1450, paper claim form.

In that replacement claim, report the claim number that Humana assigned to the claim that is being replaced, as follows:

In segment REF02 of loop 2300, using qualifier F8 in segment REF 01, of the 837 electronic transaction;

In the original ref. no. field in box 22 of the CMS-1500 paper claim form; or

As the document control number in box 64 of the UB-04, or the CMS-1450, paper claim form. Humana rejects, denies or recoups reimbursement for submissions for replacement claims when submitted outside the guidelines above. Similarly, Humana rejects, denies or recoups reimbursements for submissions that are not submitted as replacement claims, according to the guidance outlined in this policy, that Humana determines should have been submitted as replacement claims because they overlap previous claims. Any discrepancy between the data on a claim submitted previously and the data on a related replacement claim could prompt Humana to request additional information to substantiate the accuracy and completeness of the replacement claim. If Humana determines that the replacement claim is inaccurate or incomplete, it is subject to rejection, denial or recoupment. Note: For Humana Medicaid plans, this policy applies except when not permitted by state Medicaid guidelines.

extracted_content.hierarchy_path: References > Same-Claim Billing Prohibitions
extracted_content.content: Apart from same-day professional-claim services, Humana generally does not permit a provider to report charges for services furnished in multiple encounters on the same claim. definitions.title: Definitions
definitions.content:
Encounter:

For the purposes of professional claim billing discussed herein, an encounter is the entirety of one direct interaction, including a direct interaction using audio or audio and video technology, between the patient and the rendering provider, including any and all staff; or, in the absence of direct interaction between the patient and the rendering provider, the entirety of the interaction between the patient and the practitioner, including any and all staff, who ordered the services

furnished by the billing provider or who referred the patient to the billing provider. For the purposes of professional claim billing discussed herein, multiple individuals are considered one rendering provider when, due in part, for example, to common specialty, it is appropriate to bill for services furnished as though they were one rendering practitioner.

For the purposes of institutional claim billing discussed herein, an encounter is the entirety of one direct interaction between the patient and the billing provider, including any and all staff, from the first moment that relevant interaction began. Note that, for these purposes, services subject to requirements such as a three-day payment window billing requirement or a readmission same-claim billing requirement are treated as being within the meaning of "the entirety of one direct interaction."

With respect to both professional claim billing and institutional claim billing discussed herein, the phrase "any and all staff" includes, in addition to those types of persons typically referred to as staff, each person or entity engaged in the provision of services for the patient, on the provider's behalf, under any sort of agreement or arrangement with the provider.

Repetitive services: Services referred to as "defined as repetitive services" in Section 50.2.2 of Chapter 1 of the Medicare Claims Processing Manual.

extracted_content.content: A colonoscopy allows the physician to examine the lining of the entire large intestine. It is most often used as a screening procedure to look for early signs of cancer in the colon or rectum. However, the test may reveal inflamed tissue, abnormal growths and ulcers. Special instruments can be passed through the colonoscope to remove any polyps if needed. In these cases, the screening colonoscopy results in a diagnostic or therapeutic procedure. This policy describes Humana's billing expectation for distinguishing between a screening colonoscopy and a screening colonoscopy that results in a diagnostic or therapeutic procedure.

reimbursement_guidelines.title: Reimbursement Guidelines
reimbursement_guidelines.content:
In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. Humana plans may allow screening colonoscopies and screening colonoscopies that result in a diagnostic or therapeutic procedure. Members and providers should contact Humana for specific plan information.

When billing screening services, healthcare providers must report an International Classification of Diseases (ICD) diagnosis code that accurately describes the screening.

If the service begins as a screening procedure but results in a diagnostic or therapeutic procedure at the same operative session, healthcare providers should report an appropriate screening ICD diagnosis code as the primary diagnosis and the diagnostic or abnormal finding ICD diagnosis code as the secondary or subsequent diagnosis.

When a screening results in a diagnostic or therapeutic procedure, as noted above, Humana will still allow the procedure as a screening if the following conditions are met:

The member has a screening colonoscopy benefit;

The claim contains both a screening and diagnostic diagnosis code and can be supported by medical records; and

Humana Medicare Advantage (MA) plans allow Original Medicare telehealth services consistent with the applicable CMS guidance for the date of service. For dates of service beginning January 1, 2020, Humana MA plans also allow certain additional telehealth services that are not Original Medicare telehealth services. Additional telehealth services must meet the following criteria:

The service must be provided by a physician or other qualified healthcare practitioner that has satisfied Humana's telehealth credentialing and recredentialing standards and has a valid and effective contract with Humana.

The service must be provided by a physician or other qualified healthcare practitioner that satisfies the following requirements:

Services not meeting the criteria outlined above will not be allowed by Humana as additional telehealth services. Unless prohibited by applicable federal statute or regulation, Humana plans allow additional telehealth services if it is medically appropriate to furnish the service via telecommunications-based technology, the service is coverable by the plan, and all applicable coding requirements are satisfied. For further information on the service codes that may be reported as additional telehealth services, see the Medicare Advantage Additional Telehealth Services Benefit Code List section of the policy. Physicians are responsible for supervising any additional telehealth services provided to Humana MA members by nonphysician practitioners within their practices to ensure that such services conform in all respects to the requirements set forth herein.

Humana requires a provider report the POS code for an additional telehealth service as outlined below. For dates of service beginning January 1, 2024, a provider must report one of the following, as appropriate:

The applicable hospital POS code, if the patient is at home and the physician or other qualified healthcare practitioner is in the hospital, with modifier 93 or modifier 95 For dates of service from May 12, 2023, through December 31, 2023, a provider must report one of the following, as appropriate:

The POS code that would have been reported had the service been furnished in person with modifier 93

The POS code that would have been reported had the service been furnished in person with modifier 95 Note: The POS code billed for a service will determine whether that service is reimbursed with a facility or nonfacility rate.

Humana requires a provider to identify an audio-only service with modifier 93. Medicare Advantage Additional Telehealth Services Benefit Code List The attached lists of procedure codes serve as a guide to assist providers in determining which services may be reimbursable under Humana's MA additional telehealth services benefit. Click here* to view the attached code list for the applicable year.

*This document must be downloaded, saved as a PDF and opened in Adobe Acrobat to display attached files.

Humana MA plans also allow other virtual services that are covered by Original Medicare but are not Original Medicare telehealth services. These include, but are not limited to, e-visits, virtual check-ins and remote monitoring. Humana requires a provider to submit a charge for a virtual service covered by Original Medicare according to the applicable CMS guidance. Humana MA plans allow such services consistent with the applicable CMS guidance. Humana MA plans deny charges for such services that do not satisfy the applicable CMS guidance.

Specific Requirements for Claims Submitted by Federally Qualified Health Centers and Rural Health Clinics A Federally Qualified Health Center (FQHC) or Rural Health Clinic (RHC) reporting an Original Medicare telehealth service, additional telehealth service, or other virtual service should follow the applicable CMS guidance for the date of service. This includes, but is not limited to, the following guidance for reporting the correct procedure code for the service:

An Original Medicare telehealth service or additional telehealth service should be reported according to the applicable CMS guidance for the date of service, as follows: o For dates of service beginning October 1, 2026, FQHC and RHC providers should report the service using the same service code as professional providers. For the service to be allowed as an Original Medicare telehealth service, it must be on CMS's List of Telehealth Services. For the service to be allowed as an additional telehealth service, it must be on the attached list of services that may be reimbursable under Humana's additional telehealth services benefit for the applicable year. o For dates of service through September 30, 2026, reporting requirements differ based on whether the service was a mental health service. FQHC and RHC providers should report a mental health service using the same service code as professional providers. For the service to be allowed as an Original Medicare telehealth service, it must be on CMS's List of Telehealth Services. For the service to be allowed as an additional telehealth service, it must be on the attached list of services that may be reimbursable under Humana's additional telehealth services benefit for the applicable year. FQHC and RHC providers should report a service that was not a mental health service with HCPCS code G2025.

Another virtual service that is covered by Original Medicare but is not an Original Medicare telehealth service, as described above, should be reported according to the applicable CMS guidance for the date of service, as follows. o For dates of service beginning January 1, 2026, FQHC and RHC providers should report the virtual service using the same service code as professional providers. o For dates of service through December 31, 2025, FQHC and RHC providers should report the virtual service with HCPCS code G0071. In addition, FQHC and RHC providers should append modifier 93 or 95, as applicable, when reporting an Original Medicare telehealth service or additional telehealth service.

In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. Humana Medicaid plans allow telehealth services consistent with federal law and state Medicaid agency requirements.

Additional telehealth services: Telehealth services provided by an MA plan, beginning in plan year 2020, under Section 1852(m) of the Social Security Act and which are treated as a basic benefit rather than a supplemental benefit.

Electronic information and telecommunication technology: Technologies and devices which enable secure electronic communications and information exchange and typically involve the application of secure real-time audio/video conferencing or similar services, remote monitoring, or store and forward medical data technology to provide or support healthcare services.

Facility or nonfacility rate: A facility rate is the rate that would be applicable to services, under the Medicare Physician Fee Schedule (MPFS), when the patient received face-to-face services in a setting defined by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) as a facility setting. A nonfacility rate is the rate that would be applicable to services, under the MPFS, when the patient received face-to-face services in a setting defined by CMS as a nonfacility setting. A practitioner may have, for a particular procedure code, a nonfacility rate and a facility rate.

patient, or 5 minutes or more of remote evaluation of recorded video and/or images by an RHC or FQHC practitioner, occurring in lieu of an office visit; RHC or FQHC only.

HCPCS code Q3014: Telehealth originating site facility fee.

Modifier 93: Synchronous Telemedicine Service Rendered Via Telephone or Other Real-Time Interactive Audio-Only Telecommunications System.

Modifier 95: Synchronous Telemedicine Service Rendered Via a Real-Time Interactive Audio and Video Telecommunications System.

Place of service code 10: Telehealth Provided in Patient's Home.

Telehealth services include telemedicine services and are also known as virtual visits.

reimbursement_guidelines.title: Reimbursement Guidelines
reimbursement_guidelines.content:
In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. Pursuant to 42 C.F.R. § 422.112(b)(8)(i)(B), to prevent disruption of care, Humana does not require prior authorization for basic Medicare benefits during the first 90 days of a new member's enrollment for active courses of treatment that started prior to enrollment. Humana may review the services furnished during that active course of treatment against permissible coverage criteria when determining payment. To facilitate accurate claims processing of a service that, apart from the active course of treatment exception discussed above, would normally be subject to plan prior authorization requirements, Humana has developed optional modifier or condition codes. Use of these codes may facilitate claims processing by helping Humana identify claims related to an active course of treatment for new members. We encourage each provider to follow the guidance below when submitting claims for services furnished to new enrollees of Humana MA plans other than private fee-for-service (PFFS) plans:

For a professional claim, append modifier TZ to the code reported for each service that was part of an active course of treatment during the 90-day transition period.

For an outpatient facility claim, append modifier TZ to the code reported for each service that was part of an active course of treatment during the 90-day transition period.

For an inpatient facility claim, report condition code 9T for each service that was part of an active course of treatment during the 90-day transition period. A provider must not report the modifier or condition code discussed above to bill for a service:

If the service was not furnished as part of an active course of treatment that began before the member's enrollment in the specific Humana MA plan; or

If the service was not furnished during that enrollment's transition period; or

If the service was furnished to a member of a Humana MA PFFS plan. In circumstances where a claim for a new member is submitted that may involve an active course of treatment but the provider did not append a modifier or condition code discussed above, Humana may evaluate medical record documentation included with the claim to determine whether the claim involved an active course of treatment. Note: Do not report the modifier or condition code discussed in this policy when submitting claims to Humana commercial or Humana Medicaid plans.

Condition code 9T: Service is part of an active course of treatment that began before enrollment into the member's current Humana Medicare Advantage plan and was provided during the transition period.

Course of treatment: A prescribed order or ordered course of treatment for a specific individual with a specific condition that is outlined and decided upon ahead of time with the patient and the provider. A course of treatment may but is not required to be part of a treatment plan.

Inpatient facility claim: Charges for facility services submitted on the UB-04 form, or its electronic equivalent, submitted with a type of bill code that, for Original Medicare, would be used for "Part A" payment.

extracted_content.content: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. Humana may reimburse one charge for professional TCM services per discharge if a patient requires case management when transferring from a facility setting to the community or home setting. Humana requires a provider to follow all TCM requirements as outlined in relevant Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) guidance. That includes, but is not limited to, the criteria outlined in this policy. Humana reimburses the first TCM charge received for the 30-day service period that meets all of the requirements outlined in this policy. A claim showing discharge from one of the following facility settings must be received to substantiate the necessity of the professional claim for TCM services:

extracted_content.title: Skilled nursing facility
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy > Skilled nursing facility
extracted_content.content: The services associated with the face-to-face portion of the professional TCM service must be rendered by a physician, which is limited to a medical doctor (MD) or doctor of osteopathic medicine (DO), or one of the following nonphysician practitioners (NPPs): nurse practitioner, physician assistant, clinical nurse specialist or certified nurse midwife. This includes behavioral health practitioners such as psychiatrists and psychiatric nurse practitioners. Any portions of the TCM service rendered by clinical staff must be provided under the general supervision of the billing physician or NPP and are subject to applicable state law, scope of practice requirements, and conditions for services and supplies furnished incident to the professional service of a physician or NPP. Clinical staff must meet the requirements of auxiliary personnel as defined by 42 CFR 410.26(a)(1). A qualified health care provider may render TCM services for new or established patients; the reimbursement rate for TCM codes is the same regardless of new or established patient status. Note: Humana plans may reimburse a charge for reasonable and necessary evaluation and management (E/M) services for managing clinical issues, other than E/M services provided on the date of the required TCM face-to-face visit, in addition to a TCM charge, during the 30-day service period. In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. Humana may reimburse one charge for professional TCM services per discharge if a patient requires case management when transferring from a facility setting to the community or home setting. Humana requires a provider to follow all TCM requirements as outlined in relevant Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) guidance. That includes, but is not limited to, the criteria outlined in this policy. Humana reimburses the first TCM charge received for the 30-day service period that meets all of the requirements outlined in this policy. A claim showing discharge from one of the following facility settings must be received to substantiate the necessity of the professional claim for TCM services:

The services associated with the face-to-face portion of the professional TCM service must be rendered by a physician, which is limited to a medical doctor (MD) or doctor of osteopathic medicine (DO), or one of the following nonphysician practitioners (NPPs): nurse practitioner, physician assistant, clinical nurse specialist or certified nurse midwife. This includes behavioral health practitioners such as psychiatrists and psychiatric nurse practitioners. Any portions of the TCM service rendered by clinical staff must be provided under the general supervision of the billing physician or NPP and are subject to applicable state law, scope of practice requirements, and conditions for services and supplies furnished incident to the professional service of a physician or NPP. Clinical staff must meet the requirements of auxiliary personnel as defined by 42 CFR 410.26(a)(1). A qualified health care provider may render TCM services for new or established patients; the reimbursement rate for TCM codes is the same regardless of new or established patient status. Note: Humana plans may reimburse a charge for reasonable and necessary evaluation and management (E/M) services for managing clinical issues, other than E/M services provided on the date of the required TCM face-to-face visit, in addition to a TCM charge, during the 30-day service period. Humana plans do not reimburse:

TCM services rendered by the surgeon during the postoperative period of a 10- or 90-day global surgery.

TCM services when discharge management services are provided by the same provider on the same day.

A TCM charge received after the first allowable TCM, whether from the same or different provider.

A TCM charge related to a discharge that occurs during the 29-day period after the date of an earlier discharge.

E/M services on the same date as the required TCM face-to-face visit when rendered by the same provider or group practice, regardless if an E/M modifier is reported.

A qualified health care provider must render a face-to-face visit within seven days of discharge to report CPT code 99496, or within 14 days of discharge to report CPT code 99495.

A qualified health care provider must report the place of service (POS) where the face-to-face visit was furnished. The POS must be an office, outpatient setting or the patient's place of residence. The face-to-face visit may be furnished via telehealth; in such cases, the POS code billing requirements and other provisions outlined in Humana's Telehealth and Other Virtual Services claims payment policy must be followed.

A qualified health care provider must report the date of service using the date of the face-to-face visit.

CPT code 99495: Transitional care management services with the following required elements: Communication (direct contact, telephone, electronic) with the patient and/or caregiver within 2 business days of discharge At least moderate level of medical decision making during the service period Face-to-face visit, within 14 calendar days of discharge

CPT code 99496: Transitional care management services with the following required elements: Communication (direct contact, telephone, electronic) with the patient and/or caregiver within 2 business days of discharge High level of medical decision making during the service period Face-to-face visit, within 7 calendar days of discharge

Incident to: Requirements outlined by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) that must be met for a physician or nonphysician practitioner (NPP) to bill for a service or supply provided by clinical staff.

policy_title: Z-Code® Billing for Molecular Diagnostic Testing

extracted_content.title: Overview
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Overview
extracted_content.content: The Molecular Diagnostic Services (MolDX) program maintains a coding system of Diagnostics Exchange (DEX®) Z-Codes® that identifies a specific molecular diagnostic test. This policy establishes Humana's requirements for Z-Code billing for molecular diagnostic testing.

extracted_content.title: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.hierarchy_path: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. Humana requires a provider to report a molecular diagnostic test with a unique DEX Z-Code, as assigned by MolDX, and the applicable Current Procedural Terminology (CPT®) or Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System (HCPCS) Level II code. Humana denies a molecular diagnostic test CPT or HCPCS code when it is not reported with the applicable DEX Z-Code. Providers should contact the MolDX program to register molecular diagnostic tests.
